- **Tutum sıfatlarını karıştırmak.** *Critical* (eleştirel) ile *cynical* (alaycı), *cautious* (temkinli) ile *pessimistic* (karamsar), *objective* (nesnel) ile *indifferent* (ilgisiz) aynı değildir.
- **Kendi görüşünü cevaba katmak.** Türk adaylar bazen konuya kişisel olarak katıldıkları şıkkı seçer; yalnızca metnin söylediğine bak.
## Sınav ipucu
YDS’de okuma parçalarına bağlı soruların yaklaşık üçte biri ana fikir, başlık, amaç ya da tutum sorusudur. Bu soruları ayrıntı sorularından sonra çözmek çoğu zaman daha hızlıdır, çünkü ayrıntıları okurken metnin genel yönünü zaten kavrarsın. Başlık sorusunda doğru şık genellikle metnin hem konusunu hem de yazarın vardığı sonucu yansıtır. Amaç sorusunda şıkların başındaki fiillere bak (*to warn, to compare, to argue*); metnin son cümlesi amacı çoğu zaman ele verir.

nodes.title: Amaç ve tutum kelimeleri
nodes.description: Yazarın amacını ve tutumunu anlatan fiil ve sıfatlar

exercises.question: The author ---- the importance of early education, repeating the point several times throughout the article.
options: emphasizes
refutes
conceals
postpones
dismisses
exercises.explanation: Bir noktayı makale boyunca tekrar etmek onu 'vurgulamak' demektir → 'emphasizes'. 'Dismisses' (önemsemez) ve 'refutes' (çürütür) tekrar tekrar savunulan bir fikirle çelişir.

exercises.question: Although she accepts that the plan has some benefits, the writer remains ---- about whether it will work in practice.
options: enthusiastic
skeptical
generous
confident
delighted
exercises.explanation: *Although* zıtlık kurar: bazı yararları kabul ediyor ama uygulamada işe yarayacağından 'şüpheli' → 'skeptical'. 'Enthusiastic' ve 'confident' zıtlık kurmaz, kabul edilen yararlarla aynı yöndedir.

exercises.question: The main ---- of the new policy is that it may increase costs for small businesses.
options: advantage
phenomenon
evidence
drawback
hypothesis
exercises.explanation: Maliyetleri artırmak olumsuz bir özelliktir → 'drawback' (sakınca). 'Advantage' (avantaj) cümlenin olumsuz anlamıyla çelişir.

exercises.question: Rather than simply describing the problem, the article ---- a set of practical solutions.
options: underestimates
concedes
disputes
proposes
refutes
exercises.explanation: *Rather than simply describing* sorunu anlatmanın ötesine geçildiğini gösterir; makale çözümler 'önerir' → 'proposes'. 'Refutes' ve 'disputes' çözümlere karşı çıkmak anlamına gelir.

exercises.question: The writer uses the story of a single village to ---- how climate change affects ordinary people.
options: refute
conceal
overestimate
dismiss
illustrate
exercises.explanation: Tek bir köyün hikâyesi genel bir durumu 'örneklendirmek' için kullanılır → 'illustrate'. 'Conceal' (gizlemek) ve 'refute' (çürütmek) bir örneğin işlevine uymaz.

exercises.question: Many people ---- the danger, believing that the virus was no worse than the common cold.
options: underestimated
illustrated
proposed
emphasized
acknowledged
exercises.explanation: Virüsü soğuk algınlığından kötü görmemek tehlikeyi 'hafife almak'tır → 'underestimated'. 'Acknowledged' (kabul etti) ve 'emphasized' (vurguladı) tehlikenin ciddiye alındığını anlatır.

exercises.question: Contrary to conventional ----, the study found that teenagers today read more than their parents did.
options: evidence
wisdom
trend
drawback
phenomenon
exercises.explanation: *Conventional wisdom* 'yaygın kanı' demektir; *contrary to* ile birlikte 'yaygın kanının aksine' anlamı verir → 'wisdom'. 'Conventional evidence' kalıplaşmış bir ifade değildir.

exercises.text: The author ___ that social media has made people lonelier, but offers little evidence.
exercises.translation: Yazar, sosyal medyanın insanları daha yalnız hale getirdiğini iddia ediyor ama pek az kanıt sunuyor.

exercises.question: The author’s tone is largely ----: she presents both sides of the debate without taking a position.
options: hostile
enthusiastic
neutral
pessimistic
sarcastic
exercises.explanation: İki tarafı da sunup taraf tutmamak 'tarafsız' bir tutumdur → 'neutral'. 'Hostile' (düşmanca) ve 'enthusiastic' (coşkulu) bir tarafı tutmayı gerektirir.

nodes.title: Konu cümlesi ve ana fikir
nodes.description: Paragrafın konusunu, konu cümlesini ve ana fikrini bulma

exercises.passage: For more than three centuries, farmers around Lake Turvan have grown vegetables on floating platforms made of reeds and mud. Each platform, about the size of a small room, rises and falls with the water level, so crops are never flooded during the rainy season. The decaying reeds also act as a natural fertiliser, which means that farmers rarely need to buy chemical products. In recent years, agricultural researchers have begun to study the system as a possible model for low-lying regions threatened by rising seas. Some believe that, with modern materials, similar gardens could be built on rivers and coastal lagoons around the world, providing food in places where farmland is regularly lost to floods.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the history of fishing on Lake Turvan
a traditional method of farming on floating platforms and its possible uses today
the dangers of chemical fertilisers
why rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal cities and the farmland around them
the building materials used in modern houses
exercises.explanation: Önce ilk ve son cümleye bak: ilk cümle yüzen bahçeleri tanıtıyor, son cümleler bu yöntemin bugün nerelerde kullanılabileceğini anlatıyor → 'a traditional method of farming on floating platforms and its possible uses today'. 'The dangers of chemical fertilisers' çok dar bir ayrıntıdır (gübre yalnızca bir cümlede geçer); balıkçılık tarihinden söz eden şık metinde hiç geçmez.

exercises.passage: For more than three centuries, farmers around Lake Turvan have grown vegetables on floating platforms made of reeds and mud. Each platform, about the size of a small room, rises and falls with the water level, so crops are never flooded during the rainy season. The decaying reeds also act as a natural fertiliser, which means that farmers rarely need to buy chemical products. In recent years, agricultural researchers have begun to study the system as a possible model for low-lying regions threatened by rising seas. Some believe that, with modern materials, similar gardens could be built on rivers and coastal lagoons around the world, providing food in places where farmland is regularly lost to floods.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Farmers around Lake Turvan cannot grow vegetables during the rainy season.
Chemical fertilisers are too expensive for most farmers.
Floating gardens were invented by agricultural researchers.
An old farming technique from Lake Turvan may offer solutions for flood-prone regions.
Reeds are still the best and cheapest material for building modern floating platforms today.
exercises.explanation: Ana fikir = konu (yüzen bahçeler) + yazarın söylediği (sele açık bölgeler için model olabilir) → 'An old farming technique from Lake Turvan may offer solutions for flood-prone regions.' Yağmurlu mevsimde sebze yetiştirilemediğini söyleyen şık metinle çelişir (ürünler hiç su altında kalmaz); 'invented by agricultural researchers' diyen şık da çelişir, çünkü yöntem üç yüzyıllıktır, araştırmacılar onu yalnızca inceliyor.

exercises.passage: ----. In the mountain village of Saro, for example, the arrival of a single paved road in 2005 allowed farmers to sell their fruit in the city for the first time, and household incomes nearly doubled within five years. Children were able to travel to secondary schools in the next valley, and a small clinic opened because doctors could now reach the village easily. Even the local language changed, as young people began to use words they heard in the market town. Researchers who have studied Saro for two decades argue that few investments have such wide-ranging effects as a simple road, and they urge governments to give rural roads a higher priority in their budgets.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most suitable first sentence (topic sentence) for the passage?
options: Improved transport links can transform almost every aspect of life in isolated rural communities.
Building roads in remote mountainous areas is extremely expensive and often takes many years to complete.
Many villages in the region have their own languages.
Fruit farming is the main economic activity in most valleys.
Doctors are often unwilling to work in remote areas.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf *for example* ile başlıyor; demek ki ilk cümle Saro'nun örnek olduğu genel bir iddia olmalı. Yol; gelir, eğitim, sağlık ve dil üzerinde etkili olmuş → 'Improved transport links can transform almost every aspect of life …'. Yol yapımının maliyetinden, köylerin dillerinden ya da meyve tarımından söz eden şıklar tek bir yöne odaklanır ve son cümledeki 'geniş kapsamlı etkiler' fikriyle örtüşmez.

the local language of Saro has disappeared completely
Saro’s clinic was built before the road

exercises.passage: Artificial light at night is usually discussed as a problem for astronomers, who find it increasingly difficult to observe faint stars. However, a five-year study carried out in the Delvar region suggests that its most serious victims may be insects. Researchers compared fields lit by streetlamps with nearby fields that remained dark. In the lit areas, the number of moths visiting flowers at night fell by nearly 60 percent, and the plants that depend on them produced far fewer seeds. Because many birds and bats feed on these insects, the effects spread through the entire food chain. The authors conclude that reducing unnecessary outdoor lighting could be one of the cheapest ways to protect biodiversity.
exercises.question: What is the passage mainly concerned with?
options: the difficulties astronomers face
the design of modern streetlamps
the harmful effects of artificial night lighting on insects and ecosystems
the feeding habits of bats
the rising cost of street and outdoor lighting for local councils and private households
exercises.explanation: İlk cümle yaygın görüşü (gökbilimciler) verir; *However* sonrası asıl konu gelir: böcekler ve besin zinciri → 'the harmful effects of artificial night lighting on insects and ecosystems'. 'The difficulties astronomers face' yazarın geride bıraktığı yaygın görüştür; yarasaların beslenmesinden söz eden şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.

exercises.passage: It was once widely believed that raising children with two languages would confuse them and slow their development. Parents were sometimes advised to speak only the majority language at home. Over the past few decades, however, this view has been largely abandoned. A long-term study of 1,200 children in the port city of Velmora found that bilingual pupils performed at least as well as their monolingual classmates in reading and mathematics. More strikingly, they scored higher on tasks that required them to switch quickly between different rules. The researchers suggest that constantly managing two languages may train the brain’s ability to control attention. Although they caution that the benefits are modest, they argue that there is no scientific reason to discourage bilingual parenting.
exercises.question: The passage mainly argues that ----.
options: bilingual children perform worse in mathematics
parents should speak only the majority language at home
the port city of Velmora has excellent schools where children learn several foreign languages
attention problems are common among children
growing up with two languages does not harm children and may even bring some benefits
exercises.explanation: İlk cümle eski görüşü verir, *however* ile bu görüşün terk edildiği söylenir → ana fikir 'growing up with two languages does not harm children and may even bring some benefits'. 'Parents should speak only the majority language at home' metnin çürüttüğü eski tavsiyedir; 'bilingual children perform worse in mathematics' çalışmanın bulgusuyla çelişir.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?

The History of Velmora’s Port

exercises.passage: In the eighteenth century, the small trading town of Ashbury Mere had more coffee houses than churches. Historians have long treated these establishments as places of leisure, but recently discovered account books suggest that they played a much more serious role. Merchants used the coffee houses to read shipping news, sign contracts and even arrange insurance for their cargo. Some owners kept lists of ships and their expected arrival dates, which customers could consult for a small fee. In effect, the coffee houses functioned as the town’s first financial exchange, decades before an official one was established. The account books therefore force historians to reconsider the origins of commercial life in the region.
exercises.question: The main point of the passage is that ----.
options: Ashbury Mere had more churches than coffee houses
coffee was an expensive luxury in the eighteenth century
historians have finally identified the original owners of almost all the coffee houses in the town
new evidence shows that coffee houses in Ashbury Mere served as early centres of business
an official financial exchange was set up before the coffee houses opened
exercises.explanation: İkinci cümledeki *but* dönüşü ana fikri verir: hesap defterleri kahvehanelerin ciddi bir ticari rol oynadığını gösteriyor → 'coffee houses in Ashbury Mere served as early centres of business'. Kiliselerin kahvehanelerden fazla olduğunu söyleyen şık metinle çelişir; 'an official financial exchange was set up before the coffee houses opened' de çelişir, çünkü resmî borsa kahvehanelerden 'on yıllar sonra' kurulmuştur.

'The leisure activities of eighteenth-century merchants' tarihçilerin eski görüşüdür ve metin bu görüşe karşı çıkar; 'the rise of the insurance industry in Europe' aşırı geniştir, metin Avrupa'dan değil tek bir kasabadan söz eder.

exercises.passage: Over the last decade, voice-controlled home assistants have moved from novelty to necessity in millions of households. Owners praise their convenience: lights, heating and shopping lists can all be managed without lifting a finger. Yet few users stop to consider how much information these devices collect. A recent analysis of the popular Lumio assistant found that it recorded and stored short audio clips far more often than its manufacturer had claimed, sometimes when no command had been given at all. Such data, once stored, can be hacked, sold or requested by authorities. Before inviting yet another listening device into their homes, consumers would be wise to read the privacy settings carefully and switch off any features they do not need.
exercises.question: The author’s main purpose in writing the passage is to ----.
options: advertise the Lumio home assistant
explain how voice recognition technology works
describe the history of home assistants from the first models to today’s devices
warn readers about the privacy risks of voice-controlled devices
argue that home assistants should be banned
exercises.explanation: Amaç için son cümleye bak: yazar tüketicilere gizlilik ayarlarını okumalarını tavsiye ediyor; *Yet* sonrası riskleri anlatıyor → 'uyarmak' ('warn readers about the privacy risks …'). 'Argue that home assistants should be banned' aşırıdır: yazar yasak değil dikkat öneriyor; 'advertise the Lumio home assistant' metnin eleştirel tonuyla çelişir.

exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards voice-controlled home assistants can best be described as ----.
options: cautious
enthusiastic
indifferent
hostile
nostalgic
exercises.explanation: Yazar cihazların kolaylığını kabul ediyor ama dikkatli kullanılmasını öneriyor → 'cautious' (temkinli). 'Hostile' (düşmanca) fazla serttir, çünkü yazar cihazları reddetmiyor; 'enthusiastic' ise uyarı tonuyla çelişir.

exercises.passage: Teachers in the neighbouring provinces of Arlen and Morro take very different approaches to teaching young children to read. In Arlen, pupils spend their first year learning the sounds of letters and combining them into words, and stories are introduced only once these basics are secure. In Morro, by contrast, children are surrounded by picture books from the first day and are encouraged to guess words from context and illustrations. By the age of nine, children in both provinces read equally well. Arlen’s pupils, however, tend to be better at spelling, while Morro’s pupils report enjoying reading more. Each method, it seems, has its own strengths, and teachers in both provinces could probably learn something from their neighbours.
exercises.question: The primary purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: prove that Arlen’s method is superior
criticise teachers in Morro for ignoring spelling
compare two methods of teaching reading and their results
explain why children in Arlen dislike reading more than children in Morro do
persuade parents to move to Morro
exercises.explanation: *By contrast*, *however*, *while* gibi karşılaştırma işaretleri ve 'her yöntemin güçlü yanları var' sonucu amacın karşılaştırma olduğunu gösterir → 'compare two methods of teaching reading and their results'. 'Prove that Arlen's method is superior' yanlıştır, çünkü yazar iki yöntemden birini üstün tutmuyor.

exercises.question: The author’s tone in the passage is mainly ----.
options: sarcastic
angry
pessimistic
enthusiastic
objective
exercises.explanation: Yazar iki yöntemin sonuçlarını taraf tutmadan veriyor ve her birinin güçlü yanı olduğunu söylüyor → 'objective' (nesnel). 'Enthusiastic' için yazarın bir yöntemi coşkuyla savunması gerekirdi.

exercises.passage: Advertisements for brain-training apps promise a great deal. Ten minutes of puzzles a day, they claim, will sharpen memory, improve concentration and even delay the effects of ageing. The evidence for these claims, however, is remarkably thin. In most studies, users certainly become better at the specific games they practise, but these improvements rarely carry over to everyday tasks such as remembering appointments or following a conversation. One widely publicised trial of the MindLift app, often quoted in its advertising, involved only forty participants and lasted just three weeks. Until larger and more rigorous studies are carried out, consumers should treat such promises with considerable suspicion.
exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards the claims made by brain-training apps is ----.
options: supportive
enthusiastic
indifferent
admiring
skeptical
exercises.explanation: Değer bildiren kelimelere bak: *remarkably thin*, *considerable suspicion* → yazar iddialara 'şüpheyle' yaklaşıyor → 'skeptical'. 'Indifferent' (ilgisiz) yanlıştır, çünkü yazar açıkça bir görüş bildiriyor.

exercises.question: The author mentions the MindLift trial in order to ----.
options: show that the app is highly effective
illustrate how weak the evidence behind such claims can be
explain how the app was designed
recommend the app to older readers
compare different brain-training apps that are popular among older adults
exercises.explanation: Deneme yalnızca kırk kişiyle ve üç hafta sürmüş; yazar bunu kanıtların zayıflığına örnek olarak veriyor → 'illustrate how weak the evidence behind such claims can be'. 'Show that the app is highly effective' yazarın amacının tam tersidir.

exercises.passage: Coral reefs are often described as doomed, and there is no denying the scale of the damage caused by warming seas. Yet recent work off the coast of the island of Pellam offers genuine cause for hope. Marine biologists there have placed hundreds of clay structures, produced with 3D printers, on damaged sections of reef. Within four years, young corals had settled on more than seventy percent of the structures, and fish populations in the area had nearly tripled. The method is cheap, uses local materials and can be learned quickly by local divers. While it cannot solve the underlying problem of rising temperatures, it shows that damaged reefs are far from beyond repair.
exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards the Pellam project is best described as ----.
options: dismissive
optimistic
suspicious
indifferent
bitter
exercises.explanation: *Genuine cause for hope* ve *far from beyond repair* ifadeleri yazarın 'iyimser' olduğunu gösterir → 'optimistic'. 'Dismissive' (küçümseyici) ve 'suspicious' (kuşkulu) bu olumlu ifadelerle çelişir.

options: to show that the Pellam project has failed

to argue that 3D printing is too expensive
to acknowledge a limitation of the method while still supporting it
to explain how corals settle on clay structures

'To show that the Pellam project has failed' yanlıştır; yazar projenin başarısız olduğunu değil, sorunun kökünü çözemeyeceğini söylüyor. '3D printing is too expensive' diyen şık da çelişir, çünkü yöntem 'ucuz' olarak anlatılıyor.

exercises.passage: Several rural districts in the Kelmar Plains have recently moved to a four-day school week in order to save money on transport and heating. Supporters point out that teachers are less tired and that staff attendance has improved. These benefits are real, but they come at a high price. Pupils in four-day districts now spend fewer hours in class each year, and test results in mathematics have already begun to fall. Working parents, meanwhile, must find and pay for childcare on the fifth day, a burden that falls hardest on poorer families. Saving money is important, but it should not be done at the expense of children’s education. Districts that have adopted the shorter week should reconsider their decision.
exercises.question: The author’s main purpose is to ----.
options: argue that districts should return to a five-day school week
describe how rural schools save money on heating
praise teachers for their improved attendance
explain why test results in mathematics have risen
compare the school systems of several different countries around the world
exercises.explanation: Son cümle açık bir çağrıdır: kısa haftayı benimseyen bölgeler kararlarını yeniden düşünmeli → yazar ikna etmeye çalışıyor ('argue that districts should return to a five-day school week'). Matematik sonuçlarının yükseldiğini söyleyen şık metinle çelişir (sonuçlar düşüyor); ısınmada tasarruftan söz eden şık yalnızca bir ayrıntıdır.

exercises.passage: In many cities, rooftop beehives have become a symbol of environmental awareness. Hotels, banks and universities proudly advertise their own honey, and amateur beekeeping courses are frequently fully booked. It might seem obvious that more bees are good news for nature. A growing number of ecologists, however, argue that the boom in urban beekeeping may in fact be harming wild pollinators. Honeybees are managed animals, kept in large colonies of up to 50,000 individuals, and they compete with hundreds of species of wild bees for the same limited supply of flowers. A survey of the city of Harlow Bay found that in districts with the highest density of hives, wild bee numbers had fallen by almost a third over ten years. The researchers stress that honeybees are not the enemy; rather, they suggest that cities should focus on planting more flowers instead of simply adding more hives.
exercises.question: The main idea of the passage is that ----.
options: urban beekeeping courses are too expensive
honeybees should be removed from all cities
the popularity of rooftop hives may be bad for wild bees, so cities should plant more flowers
wild bees produce more and better honey than the honeybees kept in rooftop hives across the city
companies keep bees mainly for advertising
exercises.explanation: *However* sonrası ana iddiayı verir (kent arıcılığı yabani arılara zarar verebilir), son cümle de çözümü (daha çok çiçek) → 'the popularity of rooftop hives may be bad for wild bees, so cities should plant more flowers'. 'Honeybees should be removed from all cities' aşırıdır: araştırmacılar bal arılarının 'düşman olmadığını' açıkça söylüyor; 'companies keep bees mainly for advertising' yalnızca girişteki bir ayrıntıdan çıkarılmış bir yorumdur.

exercises.passage: Textbooks in the republic of Teral have long described the founding of its capital as the work of a single visionary ruler, Queen Ismene, who is said to have chosen the site in 1412 after a dream. The story is charming, and it has been repeated in schools for generations. Unfortunately, there is little evidence to support it. Tax records from the period show that a settlement already existed on the site at least eighty years earlier, and letters written by merchants describe a busy market town long before Ismene came to power. What the queen did do was build the city walls and move her court there, which may explain why later chroniclers gave her all the credit. Recognising this does not diminish her importance; it simply restores the many ordinary people who built the city to their proper place in its history.
exercises.question: The author’s main purpose in the passage is to ----.
options: challenge a popular account of how Teral’s capital was founded
praise Queen Ismene as a visionary ruler
describe the architecture of the city walls
explain why dreams were so important in medieval politics and religion
argue that textbooks should not teach history
exercises.explanation: *Unfortunately, there is little evidence to support it* cümlesiyle yazar yaygın hikâyeye karşı çıkıyor ve yeni kanıtlar sunuyor → 'challenge a popular account of how Teral's capital was founded'. 'Praise Queen Ismene as a visionary ruler' yazarın sorguladığı görüştür; 'argue that textbooks should not teach history' aşırı bir genellemedir.

options: contemptuous

exercises.passage: When remote work became common, many commentators predicted that small towns would be revived by an influx of city professionals. In some places this has happened. The mountain town of Varo, for instance, has gained nearly 2,000 new residents since 2020, and several closed shops have reopened as cafés and co-working spaces. Yet the arrival of wealthier newcomers has also pushed up house prices, and many young local people can no longer afford to live where they grew up. Local businesses report that the new residents do spend money, but they often order goods online rather than buying from local shops. The experience of Varo suggests that remote work can bring life back to small towns, but only if local authorities plan carefully for its side effects.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Remote work has had no effect on small towns.
Young people in Varo prefer to live in cities.
City professionals rarely move to small towns, even when they are allowed to work from home every day.
Remote work can revive small towns, but its benefits come with problems that need careful planning.
House prices in Varo have fallen since 2020.
exercises.explanation: Son cümle ana fikri özetler: uzaktan çalışma küçük kasabaları canlandırabilir ama yan etkileri için plan gerekir → 'Remote work can revive small towns, but its benefits come with problems …'. 'Young people in Varo prefer to live in cities' metinle çelişir: gençler istedikleri için değil, ev alamadıkları için gidiyor; 'House prices in Varo have fallen' de çelişir, fiyatlar yükseldi.

Yet the arrival of wealthier newcomers has also pushed up house prices, and many young local people can no longer afford to live where they grew up. Local businesses report that the new residents do spend money, but they often order goods online rather than buying from local shops. The experience of Varo suggests that remote work can bring life back to small towns, but only if local authorities plan carefully for its side effects.
exercises.question: The author mentions that new residents often order goods online in order to ----.
options: praise their modern lifestyle
show that their arrival does not benefit local businesses as much as expected
explain why house prices have risen
suggest that local shops should close because most residents now prefer to order goods online
prove that commentators were completely wrong
exercises.explanation: Bu ayrıntı *Yet* ile başlayan olumsuz yanlar arasında yer alır: yeni gelenler yerel dükkânlardan beklenen kadar alışveriş yapmıyor → 'show that their arrival does not benefit local businesses as much as expected'. 'Prove that commentators were completely wrong' aşırıdır; yazar yorumcuların kısmen haklı çıktığını da kabul ediyor (*In some places this has happened*).

exercises.passage: Supporters of laboratory-grown meat describe it as the solution to many of the world’s problems. Produced from animal cells in large steel tanks, it requires no farms, no slaughter and, in theory, far less land and water than conventional livestock. These advantages are real, and it would be foolish to dismiss the technology. Nevertheless, some of the more enthusiastic claims deserve closer scrutiny. The tanks must be kept at a constant temperature and free of bacteria, which requires large amounts of energy. If that energy comes from fossil fuels, the climate benefits may be much smaller than advertised. Production costs also remain high, and it is not yet clear whether consumers will accept the product. Laboratory-grown meat may well play a role in the future of food, but it is unlikely to be the miracle its promoters describe.
exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards laboratory-grown meat is best described as ----.
options: cautiously open
wholly enthusiastic
completely dismissive
indifferent
angry
exercises.explanation: Yazar avantajları 'gerçek' buluyor ve teknolojiyi reddetmenin 'aptalca' olacağını söylüyor, ama abartılı iddialara karşı uyarıyor → 'cautiously open' (temkinli biçimde açık). 'Completely dismissive' ve 'wholly enthusiastic' iki uçtur ve metinle çelişir.

exercises.passage: Supporters of laboratory-grown meat describe it as the solution to many of the world’s problems. Produced from animal cells in large steel tanks, it requires no farms, no slaughter and, in theory, far less land and water than conventional livestock. These advantages are real, and it would be foolish to dismiss the technology. Nevertheless, some of the more enthusiastic claims deserve closer scrutiny. The tanks must be kept at a constant temperature and free of bacteria, which requires large amounts of energy. If that energy comes from fossil fuels, the climate benefits may be much smaller than advertised. Production costs also remain high, and it is not yet clear whether consumers will accept the product. Laboratory-grown meat may well play a role in the future of food, but it is unlikely to be the miracle its promoters describe.
exercises.question: The author’s main purpose is to ----.
options: explain in great detail how laboratory-grown meat is produced in large steel tanks
persuade readers to stop eating meat
prove that laboratory-grown meat is harmful to health
provide a balanced assessment of the claims made for laboratory-grown meat
advertise a new food company
exercises.explanation: Yazar önce avantajları kabul ediyor, *Nevertheless* ile sorunları sıralıyor ve dengeli bir sonuca varıyor → 'provide a balanced assessment of the claims made for laboratory-grown meat'. Çelik tanklarda üretimi anlatan şık metinde geçen bir ayrıntıdır ama amaç değildir; 'prove that laboratory-grown meat is harmful to health' metinde hiç ele alınmaz, sorunlar sağlıkla değil enerji ve maliyetle ilgilidir.

exercises.passage: On the steep, forested island of Merrin, villagers developed a remarkable way of communicating across deep valleys: a whistled form of their spoken language. By changing the pitch and length of their whistles, speakers could send detailed messages over distances of up to three kilometres, far beyond the reach of a shouting voice. For centuries, the whistled language was essential for farmers and shepherds working on opposite slopes. When mobile phones arrived in the 1990s, however, young people saw little reason to learn it, and by 2010 only a few dozen elderly speakers remained. Since then, the island’s schools have introduced weekly whistling lessons, and a small but growing number of children can now hold simple conversations. Linguists hope the revival will preserve not only a communication system but also a unique part of the island’s identity.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: Mobile Phones Reach Merrin
Farming on Steep Slopes
How Sound Travels in Valleys
The Elderly Population of Merrin
Saving Merrin’s Whistled Language
exercises.explanation: Metin ıslıklı dilin ortaya çıkışını, gerilemesini ve canlandırılmasını anlatıyor; başlık bu bütünü kapsamalı → 'Saving Merrin's Whistled Language'. 'Mobile Phones Reach Merrin' yalnızca gerilemenin sebebini, 'Farming on Steep Slopes' ise arka plandaki bir ayrıntıyı başlık yapar.

exercises.passage: On the steep, forested island of Merrin, villagers developed a remarkable way of communicating across deep valleys: a whistled form of their spoken language. By changing the pitch and length of their whistles, speakers could send detailed messages over distances of up to three kilometres, far beyond the reach of a shouting voice. For centuries, the whistled language was essential for farmers and shepherds working on opposite slopes. When mobile phones arrived in the 1990s, however, young people saw little reason to learn it, and by 2010 only a few dozen elderly speakers remained. Since then, the island’s schools have introduced weekly whistling lessons, and a small but growing number of children can now hold simple conversations. Linguists hope the revival will preserve not only a communication system but also a unique part of the island’s identity.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why shepherds prefer mobile phones
the geography of Merrin’s forests
the decline and revival of a whistled form of language on Merrin
the way linguists record and study the sounds of endangered languages around the world
the history of schools on the island
exercises.explanation: Metnin konusu ıslıklı dilin gerilemesi ve yeniden canlanmasıdır → 'the decline and revival of a whistled form of language on Merrin'. 'The reasons why shepherds prefer mobile phones' metinle uyuşmaz (telefonu tercih edenler gençlerdir, çobanlar değil); okulların tarihinden söz eden şık yalnızca canlanma sürecindeki bir ayrıntıdır.

nodes.title: Ünite testi
nodes.description: 16 soruluk ünite testi; geçmek için %80 doğru yap

exercises.question: The report ---- the need for more investment in public transport, mentioning it in almost every chapter.
options: conceals
emphasizes
dismisses
underestimates
refutes
exercises.explanation: Bir konuyu neredeyse her bölümde anmak onu 'vurgulamak'tır → 'emphasizes'. 'Conceals' (gizler) ve 'dismisses' (önemsemez) sık sık anılan bir konuyla çelişir.

exercises.question: If the researchers ---- a larger sample, their conclusions would have been more convincing.
options: had used
use
have used
would use
are using
exercises.explanation: Ana cümlede *would have been* var → üçüncü tip koşul; if kısmı past perfect ister: 'had used'. 'Use' birinci tip koşula aittir ve *would have been* ile uyuşmaz.

exercises.passage: Many students believe that complete silence is the best condition for studying. A recent experiment at the University of Halden challenges this assumption. Participants were asked to solve creative problems while listening to silence, to quiet café sounds or to loud traffic noise. Those exposed to a moderate level of background noise solved significantly more problems than those working in silence, while loud noise reduced performance in all groups. The researchers suggest that a little noise makes the brain work slightly harder, encouraging more abstract thinking. However, they note that the effect applied only to creative tasks; for memorising facts and figures, silence remained the better option.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the architectural design of modern university libraries and their silent study rooms
how different levels of background noise affect thinking and studying
why traffic noise damages hearing
the best cafés for students
methods for memorising facts
exercises.explanation: Metin sessizlik, orta düzey ve yüksek gürültünün düşünme üzerindeki etkisini karşılaştırıyor → 'how different levels of background noise affect thinking and studying'. 'Methods for memorising facts' yalnızca son cümledeki bir ayrıntıdır; trafik gürültüsünün işitmeye zararından söz eden şık metinde hiç ele alınmaz.

exercises.passage: Many students believe that complete silence is the best condition for studying. A recent experiment at the University of Halden challenges this assumption. Participants were asked to solve creative problems while listening to silence, to quiet café sounds or to loud traffic noise. Those exposed to a moderate level of background noise solved significantly more problems than those working in silence, while loud noise reduced performance in all groups. The researchers suggest that a little noise makes the brain work slightly harder, encouraging more abstract thinking. However, they note that the effect applied only to creative tasks; for memorising facts and figures, silence remained the better option.
exercises.question: The author’s purpose in the last sentence is to ----.
options: prove that silence is always best
recommend café music for all tasks
criticise the researchers’ methods
point out a limit to the experiment’s findings
introduce a new experiment
exercises.explanation: Son cümle *However* ile etkinin yalnızca yaratıcı görevlerde geçerli olduğunu söyleyerek bulgulara bir sınır koyar → 'point out a limit to the experiment's findings'. 'Recommend café music for all tasks' tam tersidir: ezber için sessizlik daha iyi bulunmuştur; 'prove that silence is always best' ise aşırı bir genellemedir.

exercises.question: Although the author praises the government’s goals, ----.
options: she agrees with all of its methods
because the policy is popular
so the plan will succeed
she doubts whether its methods will achieve them
which were announced last year
exercises.explanation: *Although* zıtlık ister: hedefleri övüyor ama yöntemlerden şüphe ediyor → 'she doubts whether its methods will achieve them'. 'She agrees with all of its methods' övgüyle aynı yöndedir, zıtlık kurmaz; *because* ve *so* ile başlayan şıklar köke ikinci bir bağlaç ekler.

exercises.passage: Laptops are now a common sight in lecture halls, and many students find typing notes faster and more convenient than writing by hand. A study conducted at three colleges in the province of Terrin, however, suggests that speed is not always an advantage. Students who typed their notes recorded nearly twice as many words as those who wrote by hand, but they often copied the lecturer’s sentences word for word. Students who wrote by hand, forced to work more slowly, had to summarise ideas in their own words. When tested a week later, the handwriting group remembered the key concepts considerably better. The researchers conclude that the way students take notes may matter more than how much they write.
exercises.question: The best title for the passage would be ----.
options: The History of the Laptop
Why Lecturers Speak Too Fast
Slower but Smarter: The Case for Handwritten Notes
How to Type Twice as Fast
Colleges in the Province of Terrin
exercises.explanation: Başlık hem konuyu (not alma) hem de sonucu (elle yazmak daha iyi hatırlatıyor) yansıtmalı; doğru cevap 'Slower but Smarter'. 'How to Type Twice as Fast' metnin iddiasının tersine hızı öne çıkarır; 'Colleges in the Province of Terrin' yalnızca araştırmanın yerini verir.

exercises.passage: Laptops are now a common sight in lecture halls, and many students find typing notes faster and more convenient than writing by hand. A study conducted at three colleges in the province of Terrin, however, suggests that speed is not always an advantage. Students who typed their notes recorded nearly twice as many words as those who wrote by hand, but they often copied the lecturer’s sentences word for word. Students who wrote by hand, forced to work more slowly, had to summarise ideas in their own words. When tested a week later, the handwriting group remembered the key concepts considerably better. The researchers conclude that the way students take notes may matter more than how much they write.
exercises.question: The main point of the passage is that ----.
options: writing notes by hand may help students remember ideas better than typing
typing helps students record more ideas and remember them better
lecturers should ban laptops in lecture halls
students in Terrin prefer laptops to notebooks because typing allows them to write faster
handwriting is faster than typing
exercises.explanation: Son cümle ve test sonucu ana fikri verir: elle not almak kavramları daha iyi hatırlatıyor → 'writing notes by hand may help students remember ideas better than typing'. 'Typing helps students record more ideas and remember them better' metinle çelişir (yazanlar daha çok kelime kaydetti ama daha az hatırladı); laptopların yasaklanmasını öneren şık metinde yer almayan bir öneridir.

exercises.question: The writer does not deny that the project has some benefits, but he believes its costs are far greater.
options: Yazar projenin hiçbir yararı olmadığını ve maliyetlerinin çok yüksek olduğunu düşünüyor.
Yazar projenin bazı yararları olduğunu kabul ediyor ve maliyetlerinin düşük olduğuna inanıyor.
Yazar projenin bazı yararları olduğunu inkâr ediyor, ama maliyetlerinin düşük olduğunu düşünüyor.
Yazar projenin bazı yararları olduğunu kabul ediyor ve yararlarının maliyetlerinden çok daha fazla olduğuna inanıyor.
Yazar projenin bazı yararları olduğunu inkâr etmiyor, ama maliyetlerinin çok daha fazla olduğuna inanıyor.
exercises.explanation: *Does not deny* 'inkâr etmiyor', *its costs are far greater* 'maliyetlerinin çok daha fazla olduğu'; doğru çeviri 'inkâr etmiyor, ama maliyetlerinin çok daha fazla' diyendir. 'hiçbir yararı olmadığını' diyen şık *some benefits*'i 'hiçbir yararı yok' yapar; 'yararlarının maliyetlerinden çok daha fazla' diyen şık karşılaştırmanın yönünü tersine çevirir.

exercises.passage: Travellers crossing the Qaros dunes have long reported a strange low humming sound, sometimes loud enough to be heard several kilometres away. Local legends attributed the noise to spirits living beneath the sand. Scientists now offer a more practical explanation. When a layer of dry sand slides down the steep face of a dune, the grains rub against one another in a regular rhythm, and the whole layer vibrates like the skin of a drum. Only sand grains of a certain size and shape, polished smooth by the wind, produce the effect, which is why most dunes remain silent. Recordings made at Qaros show that the dunes ‘sing’ most often on hot, dry afternoons, when the sand is loosest.
exercises.question: The primary purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: argue that local legends are dangerous
persuade travellers to visit the Qaros dunes
compare different deserts of the world
explain the cause of a natural phenomenon
describe the life of desert spirits
exercises.explanation: Metin kumulların neden 'şarkı söylediğini' bilimsel olarak açıklıyor → 'explain the cause of a natural phenomenon'. 'Argue that local legends are dangerous' yanlıştır: efsaneler yalnızca anılır, tehlikeli oldukları söylenmez; 'compare different deserts of the world' aşırı geniştir, metin tek bir kumul alanından söz eder.

exercises.passage: Travellers crossing the Qaros dunes have long reported a strange low humming sound, sometimes loud enough to be heard several kilometres away. Local legends attributed the noise to spirits living beneath the sand. Scientists now offer a more practical explanation. When a layer of dry sand slides down the steep face of a dune, the grains rub against one another in a regular rhythm, and the whole layer vibrates like the skin of a drum. Only sand grains of a certain size and shape, polished smooth by the wind, produce the effect, which is why most dunes remain silent. Recordings made at Qaros show that the dunes ‘sing’ most often on hot, dry afternoons, when the sand is loosest.
exercises.question: The tone of the passage is best described as ----.
options: mocking
informative
angry
sentimental
pessimistic
exercises.explanation: Yazar bir olguyu nedenleriyle, duygusal ifadeler kullanmadan açıklıyor → 'informative' (bilgilendirici). 'Mocking' (alaycı) yanlıştır; efsaneler alaya alınmaz, yalnızca bilimsel açıklamayla karşılaştırılır.

exercises.question: Makalenin amacı okuyucuları yeni bir ilaç hakkında uyarmaktır.
options: The aim of the article is to persuade readers to try a new drug.
The article warned readers about an old drug.
The aim of the article is to warn readers about a new drug.
The aim of the article was to inform doctors about a new drug.
Readers warned the author of the article about a new drug.
exercises.explanation: 'Amacı … uyarmaktır' → *The aim … is to warn*; doğru cevap 'The aim of the article is to warn readers…'. 'persuade' diyen şık amacı 'ikna etmek' yapar; 'inform doctors' diyen şık okuyucuyu 'doktor', zamanı geçmiş yapar; 'Readers warned the author' diyen şık özne ile nesneyi yer değiştirir.

exercises.passage: A new kind of travel has become popular in recent years: so-called last-chance tourism, in which visitors rush to see glaciers, coral reefs and other natural wonders before they disappear. Tour operators present such trips as a way to raise awareness of environmental damage. There is, however, an obvious contradiction. The long-haul flights that carry tourists to the melting glaciers of the Sarn Mountains produce large amounts of greenhouse gases, contributing to the very warming that threatens the ice. Local communities do benefit from the income, but much of the money goes to international companies. Travellers who genuinely care about these places might do more good by staying at home and supporting conservation projects directly.
exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards last-chance tourism is mainly ----.
options: critical
enthusiastic
neutral
amused
uncertain
exercises.explanation: *An obvious contradiction* ifadesi ve son cümledeki 'evde kalmak daha yararlı olabilir' önerisi yazarın eleştirel olduğunu gösterir → 'critical'. 'Neutral' yanlıştır, çünkü yazar açıkça bir görüş bildiriyor.

exercises.passage: A new kind of travel has become popular in recent years: so-called last-chance tourism, in which visitors rush to see glaciers, coral reefs and other natural wonders before they disappear. Tour operators present such trips as a way to raise awareness of environmental damage. There is, however, an obvious contradiction. The long-haul flights that carry tourists to the melting glaciers of the Sarn Mountains produce large amounts of greenhouse gases, contributing to the very warming that threatens the ice. Local communities do benefit from the income, but much of the money goes to international companies. Travellers who genuinely care about these places might do more good by staying at home and supporting conservation projects directly.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Glaciers in the Sarn Mountains are growing.
Tour operators donate most of their profits to local communities.
Long-haul flights are cheaper than ever before.
Coral reefs are now more popular with last-chance tourists than melting glaciers are.
Last-chance tourism may harm the very places it claims to celebrate.
exercises.explanation: Metnin merkezindeki çelişki: turistleri buzullara taşıyan uçuşlar buzu eriten ısınmaya katkıda bulunuyor → 'Last-chance tourism may harm the very places it claims to celebrate.' 'Glaciers in the Sarn Mountains are growing' metinle çelişir (buzullar eriyor); kârların yerel halka bağışlandığını söyleyen şık da çelişir, paranın çoğu uluslararası şirketlere gidiyor.

exercises.question: It is not so much the cost of the treatment as its side effects that worries doctors.
options: Doctors are worried mainly about the cost of the treatment, not its side effects.
What worries doctors is the side effects of the treatment rather than its cost.
Doctors are not worried about either the cost or the side effects of the treatment.
The treatment is both expensive and harmful, according to doctors.
Doctors believe the side effects of the treatment are less serious than its cost.
exercises.explanation: *Not so much X as Y* 'X'ten çok Y' demektir: doktorları asıl kaygılandıran yan etkiler → 'What worries doctors is the side effects of the treatment rather than its cost.' Kaygının asıl maliyet olduğunu söyleyen şık ile yan etkileri maliyetten daha az ciddi bulan şık ilişkiyi tersine çevirir; 'not worried about either' diyen şık her iki kaygıyı da reddeder.

exercises.passage: ----. In the coastal city of Revan, a programme that paid fishermen to collect plastic waste from the sea removed more than 400 tonnes of rubbish in just two years. The fishermen, whose catches had been falling for a decade, gained a second source of income, and some used the money to repair their boats. At the same time, the collected plastic was sold to a local company that turns it into building materials such as roof tiles and paving stones. City officials now plan to extend the scheme to river ports further inland, arguing that it solves an environmental problem and an economic one at the same time.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most suitable first sentence for the passage?
options: Fishing has been the main industry in Revan for centuries.
Plastic is one of the cheapest building materials available.
Many fishermen have left the industry because of low catches.
River ports are often far more polluted than coastal cities, which have stricter rules on waste.
Cleaning the oceans can also create new economic opportunities for coastal communities.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Revan'ı bir örnek olarak sunuyor ve son cümlede programın hem çevre hem ekonomi sorununu çözdüğünü söylüyor; bu iki yönü birden kapsayan genel cümle 'Cleaning the oceans can also create new economic opportunities…' cümlesidir. Balıkçıların sektörü bıraktığını söyleyen şık yalnızca balıkçılara, plastiğin ucuzluğundan söz eden şık yalnızca plastiğe odaklanır ve paragrafın bütününü tanıtmaz.

exercises.passage: ----. In the coastal city of Revan, a programme that paid fishermen to collect plastic waste from the sea removed more than 400 tonnes of rubbish in just two years. The fishermen, whose catches had been falling for a decade, gained a second source of income, and some used the money to repair their boats. At the same time, the collected plastic was sold to a local company that turns it into building materials such as roof tiles and paving stones. City officials now plan to extend the scheme to river ports further inland, arguing that it solves an environmental problem and an economic one at the same time.
exercises.question: The author’s attitude towards the Revan programme is ----.
options: disapproving
doubtful
approving
indifferent
sarcastic
exercises.explanation: Yazar programın sonuçlarını yalnızca olumlu yönleriyle aktarıyor ve iki sorunu birden çözdüğünü vurguluyor → 'approving' (onaylayan). 'Doubtful' yanlıştır, çünkü metinde hiçbir çekince ya da eleştiri yok.
