Their environmental benefits, however, are less clear than they first appear. ---- In addition, early models lasted less than a year before they had to be replaced, so the emissions produced in manufacturing them were spread over very few journeys. Newer, more durable models and changes in how scooters are collected may improve the picture. Cities that require operators to use electric vans for collection have already reported lower overall emissions.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Scooters are particularly popular among tourists.
Many scooters are collected each night by vans that drive around the city to recharge them.
Moreover, they produce no emissions at any stage of their life, from manufacture to final disposal.
As a result, many cities have banned private cars.
Electric cars are becoming cheaper every year.
exercises.explanation: Önceki cümle çevresel yararların şüpheli olduğunu söyler, sonraki cümle 'In addition' ile ikinci bir sorun ekler; boşlukta ilk sorun olmalıdır: scooter'ların her gece minibüslerle toplanması. Doğru cevap 'collected each night by vans'; son cümledeki 'how scooters are collected' de bunu destekler. 'they produce no emissions at any stage' diyen şık paragrafın iddiasıyla çelişir; 'particularly popular among tourists' diyen şık ise sorun bildirmez.

exercises.passage: ---- For centuries, the people of the Orrin Highlands built their houses with thick stone walls and small windows, which kept interiors cool in summer and retained heat in winter. In the 1970s, many of these homes were replaced by concrete buildings with large windows, which required air conditioning in summer and heavy heating in winter. Today, architects in the region are rediscovering the old techniques and combining them with modern insulation. The resulting homes use up to 60 percent less energy than the concrete buildings they replaced.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Concrete is one of the most widely used building materials in the world, especially in large cities.
As a result, air conditioning was never used in the highlands.
Large windows always make houses warmer in winter.
Architects in the region prefer to use only modern materials.
Traditional building methods are often better adapted to local climates than modern ones.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf geleneksel taş evlerin iklime uygunluğunu, beton yapıların ise enerji gerektirdiğini karşılaştırır; ana fikri veren 'Traditional building methods are often better adapted to local climates' doğru konu cümlesidir. 'Architects ... prefer to use only modern materials' diyen şık mimarların eski teknikleri yeniden keşfettiği bilgisiyle çelişir; 'air conditioning was never used' diyen şık ise klimanın kullanıldığı bilgisine aykırıdır.

exercises.passage: For decades, conservationists focused on protecting large, charismatic animals such as tigers and elephants, partly because these species attract public donations. Ecologists have increasingly argued, however, that this approach overlooks the organisms on which entire ecosystems depend. Soil fungi, for example, help plants absorb nutrients, while insects pollinate crops and break down dead material. Yet such organisms receive only a tiny share of conservation funding. Many of these species have never even been formally described by scientists, let alone assessed for their risk of extinction. ----
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Elephants are the largest land animals on Earth.
As a result, soil fungi now receive most conservation funding.
Some researchers are therefore calling for a shift in priorities towards the less visible species that keep ecosystems functioning.
Donations from the public have increased every year.
Insects, however, are of little importance to agriculture.
exercises.explanation: Paragraf ekosistemler için hayati olan küçük canlıların fonlardan çok az pay aldığını vurgular; sonda öncelik değişikliği çağrısı yapan 'calling for a shift in priorities' mantıklı kapanıştır. 'soil fungi now receive most conservation funding' diyen şık hemen önceki 'only a tiny share' bilgisiyle çelişir; 'Insects, however, are of little importance' diyen şık böceklerin tozlaşmadaki rolüyle çelişir; 'Elephants are the largest land animals' ise doğru ama konudan sapan bir bilgidir.

nodes.title: Ünite ödülü
nodes.description: Üniteyi bitir, bonus XP kazan

units.title: Anlam bütünlüğünü bozan
units.description: Paragrafın akışını bozan, konu dışı cümleyi bulma
units.guide:
## Strateji
Bu soru tipinde (I)–(V) diye numaralandırılmış beş cümlelik bir paragraf verilir ve akışı bozan, yani **anlam bütünlüğüne uymayan** cümle sorulur. Önemli nokta şudur: aranan cümle çoğu zaman tamamen ilgisiz değildir. Genellikle paragrafla **aynı kelimeyi ya da aynı genel konuyu** paylaşır (ör. paragraf üzüm bağları ve iklim değişikliğini anlatırken şarap kadehlerinden söz eden cümle). Ancak paragrafın asıl **odağından** sapar. Bu yüzden önce paragrafın tek cümlelik ana fikrini çıkarmak, sonra her cümlenin bu ana fikre ve komşu cümlelere bağlanıp bağlanmadığını kontrol etmek gerekir. Gönderim sözcükleri (*this, these, such, they, it*), bağlaçlar (*however, therefore, in turn, instead*) ve zaman tutarlılığı (geçmişteki bir anlatının ortasında geniş zamanlı genel bir bilgi) en güçlü ipuçlarıdır.

## Örnekler
- *(IV) Undeterred, Grell spent the next ten years improving his design.* — *Undeterred* (yılmadan) bir önceki cümlede bir başarısızlık anlatılmış olmasını gerektirir.
- *(III) These baking days became important social occasions.* — *These* önceki cümledeki fırın günlerini gösterir; araya giren bir cümle bu bağı koparır.
- *(I) They were usually painted in bright colours.* — İlk cümle *They* ile başlıyorsa gösterecek isim yoktur; bu, cümlenin yerinde olmadığının işaretidir.
- *Steel is an alloy made mainly of iron.* — Köprünün tarihini anlatan paragrafta çeliğin tanımı odak dışıdır.

## Nasıl çözülür
1. İlk iki cümleyi okuyup paragrafın **konusunu ve odağını** belirle (ör. 'Arlen Köprüsü'nün tarihi', 'geceleri çalışmanın sağlığa etkisi').
2. Her cümleyi sırayla oku ve kendine sor: *Bu cümle konuyu ilerletiyor mu, yoksa yalnızca ortak bir kelime mi taşıyor?*
3. **Gönderim zincirini** takip et: *he, she, it, they, this, these, such* kimi/neyi gösteriyor? Bir cümle bu zinciri kırıyorsa ya da kendi zamiri karşılıksız kalıyorsa şüphelen.
4. **Zaman ve anlatım türünü** kontrol et: geçmiş zamanlı bir hikâyenin ortasında geniş zamanlı genel bir bilgi (*Steel is…, Dogs need…*) çoğu zaman aranan cümledir.
5. Şüphelendiğin cümleyi çıkarıp paragrafı yeniden oku. Akış düzgünleşiyor ve bağlaçlar (*however, then, as a result*) doğru yerlere bağlanıyorsa cevap odur.

**Örnek çözüm:** *(I) The Brook Street Library was built in 1905. (II) For most of the century, it served as the town's main source of books. (III) In the 1990s, however, visitor numbers fell sharply. (IV) Many people prefer reading e-books because they can carry hundreds of titles. (V) Instead of closing the building, the council turned it into a community centre.*
Adım 1: Konu, kütüphanenin tarihi. Adım 3: II'deki *it* kütüphaneyi, V'teki *it* yine binayı gösterir. Adım 4: IV geçmiş zamanlı anlatının ortasında genel bir tercih bildirir. Adım 5: IV çıkarılınca III'teki ziyaretçi düşüşünden V'teki çözüme doğal bir geçiş olur. Cevap: IV.

## Tuzaklar ve sık yapılan hatalar
- **Ortak kelimeye aldanmak:** Konu dışı cümle çoğu zaman paragraftaki bir anahtar kelimeyi (*heat, salt, dogs, glass*) tekrar eder. Kelime ortaklığı, anlam ortaklığı değildir.
- **İlk cümleyi asla seçmemek:** Ana fikir genellikle ilk cümlededir, ama ÖSYM bazen konu dışı cümleyi başa koyar. İkinci cümle tek başına güçlü bir giriş cümlesi olabiliyorsa I'i de değerlendir.
- **Karşıt görüşü konu dışı sanmak:** *Critics, however, argue…* ile başlayan cümle konuya farklı bir bakış getirir ama bütünlüğü bozmaz; aksine paragrafın parçasıdır.
- **Genel doğruya güvenmek:** Cümlenin kendi başına doğru olması (*Penicillin was produced during the Second World War*) paragrafa ait olduğunu göstermez.
- **Türkçe okuma alışkanlığı:** Türkçede zamir sık düştüğü için adaylar *they, these* gibi gönderimleri gözden kaçırır. İngilizce paragrafta bu sözcükler cümleleri birbirine bağlayan halkalardır.

## Sınav ipucu
YDS'de bu tipte genellikle 5 soru gelir ve soru başına 1 dakika yeterlidir. Paragrafı okurken her cümlenin yanına zihninde tek kelimelik bir etiket koy (*tarih, neden, sonuç, örnek, öneri*); etiketi ana fikirle uyuşmayan cümle hemen göze çarpar. Paragraf geçmiş zamanla bir olayı anlatıyorsa geniş zamanlı tanım cümlesine, bir sorun–çözüm akışı varsa sorunla ilgisi olmayan tarihî bilgiye dikkat et. Emin olamazsan şüpheli cümleyi atıp kalan dört cümlenin bağlaçlarını kontrol et.

nodes.title: Bütünlük kelimeleri
nodes.description: Gönderim ve bağlantı sözcükleri ile metinlerde geçen akademik kelimeler

exercises.question: The paragraph lacks ---- because its sentences jump from one topic to another.
options: abundance
emission
sediment
fragment
coherence
exercises.explanation: Cümleleri bir konudan ötekine atlayan paragrafta eksik olan şey 'tutarlılık, anlam bütünlüğü'dür (coherence). 'Fragment' (parça) ve 'sediment' (tortu) bir paragrafın niteliği olarak anlam vermez; 'emission' ise salım demektir.

exercises.question: Engineers built a series of dams to ---- the floods, and the dams also generated electricity.
options: resemble
control
praise
reside
imitate
exercises.explanation: Barajlar selleri 'kontrol etmek' için yapılır; doğru şık 'control'. 'Resemble' (benzemek) ve 'imitate' (taklit etmek) sellerle anlamlı bir ilişki kurmaz; 'reside' ise nesne almaz.

exercises.text: The third sentence is ___ to the topic, so it breaks the flow of the paragraph.
exercises.translation: Üçüncü cümle konuyla ilgisiz, bu yüzden paragrafın akışını bozuyor.

exercises.question: In its first two years, the scheme ---- more than 30 tonnes of plastic from the surrounding waters.
options: replaced
attracted
resembled
removed
persuaded
exercises.explanation: 'remove X from Y' = X'i Y'den çıkarmak, temizlemek; program denizden plastik 'çıkarmıştır'. Doğru şık 'removed'. 'Attracted' (çekti) 'from' ile bu anlamı vermez; 'replaced' ise bir şeyin yerine başka bir şey koymaktır.

exercises.question: Without predators to control them, sea urchins can ---- an entire kelp forest in a few months.
options: strip
praise
attract
assume
reveal
exercises.explanation: Doğal düşmanı olmayan deniz kestaneleri bir yosun ormanını birkaç ayda 'çıplak bırakabilir'; 'strip' doğrudur. 'Reveal' (ortaya çıkarmak) ve 'attract' (çekmek) yok etme anlamı taşımaz.

exercises.question: Rising temperatures have caused the grapes to ---- nearly three weeks earlier than before.
options: migrate
dissolve
ripen
persuade
abandon
exercises.explanation: Sıcaklık artışı üzümlerin daha erken 'olgunlaşmasına' yol açar; 'ripen' doğrudur. 'Migrate' (göç etmek) hayvanlar için, 'dissolve' (çözünmek) maddeler için kullanılır; 'abandon' ise nesne ister.

exercises.text: Higher prices reduced demand, which ___ led to lower profits.
exercises.translation: Daha yüksek fiyatlar talebi azalttı, bu da kârların düşmesine yol açtı.

exercises.question: The dams also trapped the ---- that had once fertilised the fields along the river.
options: shoal
stem
vintage
sediment
dawn
exercises.explanation: Nehrin taşıyıp tarlaları verimli kılan şey alüvyon, yani 'sediment'tir ve barajlar onu tutar. 'Shoal' balık sürüsü, 'stem' bitki gövdesi demektir; ikisi de tarlaları gübrelemez.

exercises.question: Undeterred by the rejection, the engineer spent ten years trying to attract private ----.
options: ancestors
investors
predators
invaders
residents
exercises.explanation: Reddedilen projesi için mühendis özel 'yatırımcı' çekmeye çalışmıştır; 'attract private investors' doğal bir eşdizimdir. 'Predators' (yırtıcılar) ve 'invaders' (istilacılar) bağlama uymaz; 'ancestors' (atalar) ise çekilebilecek kişiler değildir.

nodes.title: Konu dışı ve farklı odak
nodes.description: Tamamen ilgisiz cümleyi ve aynı konuda ama farklı odaktaki cümleyi bulma

exercises.passage: (I) The Kerrin Valley vineyards have been producing wine for over three centuries, mainly from a single local grape variety. (II) Wine glasses with long stems were designed so that the drinker's hand would not warm the wine. (III) Over the past twenty years, however, rising temperatures have caused the grapes to ripen nearly three weeks earlier than before. (IV) Earlier ripening raises the sugar content of the grapes, which in turn produces stronger wines with less acidity. (V) Some growers are therefore experimenting with planting vines on higher, cooler slopes to preserve the traditional taste.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Kerrin Vadisi'ndeki üzümlerin iklim değişikliği nedeniyle erken olgunlaşmasını ve üreticilerin çözüm arayışını anlatır. II. cümle 'wine' kelimesini paylaşsa da şarap kadehlerinin tasarımına geçerek konudan kopar; doğru cevap II. III'teki 'however' I'deki uzun geleneğe bağlanır.

exercises.passage: (I) Researchers at Dalby University have developed a paint that can lower the temperature of buildings without using any electricity. (II) The paint contains tiny particles that reflect almost all incoming sunlight and release heat as infrared radiation into the sky. (III) In tests, surfaces coated with it remained up to 4°C cooler than the surrounding air even at midday. (IV) The earliest paints were made from natural materials such as charcoal, clay and crushed minerals. (V) If production costs can be reduced, the developers believe the paint could significantly cut the demand for air conditioning in hot countries.
exercises.question: Which sentence is irrelevant to the overall meaning of the passage?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf binaları serinleten yeni bir boyayı, işleyişini, test sonuçlarını ve geleceğini anlatır. IV. cümle 'paint' kelimesini tekrar eder ama tarihteki ilk boyalara geçerek odaktan sapar; doğru cevap IV. V'teki 'the paint' doğrudan III'teki test sonucunu izler.

exercises.passage: (I) Sign languages are complete natural languages with their own grammar and vocabulary, not simply gestures that accompany speech. (II) Like spoken languages, they differ from country to country, so a deaf person from one nation may not understand signers from another. (III) In the Varn Islands, a new sign language emerged within only two generations when deaf children were first brought together in a school. (IV) Linguists studying this language observed that the children, not the adults, created most of its grammatical rules. (V) Hearing loss can be caused by exposure to loud noise over long periods of time.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf işaret dillerinin gerçek diller olduğunu ve Varn Adaları'nda yeni bir işaret dilinin nasıl doğduğunu anlatır. V. cümle ise işitme kaybının nedenlerine geçer; sağırlıkla ilgili olsa da dil konusundan kopar. Doğru cevap V.

exercises.passage: (I) Coffee was traditionally served in small cups in many Mediterranean countries. (II) Over the past five years, the city of Arnhold has replaced all of its diesel buses with electric ones. (III) The change has reduced the city's transport emissions by nearly a third and made the streets noticeably quieter. (IV) Operating costs have also fallen, since electricity is cheaper than diesel and electric engines need less maintenance. (V) Other cities in the region are now studying Arnhold's experience before deciding whether to follow its example.
exercises.question: Which sentence is irrelevant to the overall meaning of the passage?
options: I
II
III
IV

Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

exercises.passage: Many people assume that a large vocabulary simply comes from studying word lists. ---- Learners who read widely meet the same words again and again in different contexts, gradually learning not only their meanings but also how they combine with other words. units.title: Okuma kampı 1: fen
units.description: Gerçek YDS uzunluğunda fen ve teknoloji metinleriyle okuma pratiği
units.guide:
## Strateji
Okuma bölümü YDS'de 20 soru, yani puanın dörtte biridir. Metinler fen, sağlık, sosyal bilimler ve tarih gibi alanlardan gelen 150–250 kelimelik akademik paragraflardır ve her metne genellikle 4 soru sorulur. Bu kampta metinler gerçek sınav uzunluğundadır; ilk metinler daha kısa ve sade, son ders ve ünite testi tam sınav düzeyindedir. Fen ve teknoloji metinleri genellikle aynı iskeleti izler: **sorun → yeni yöntem/deney → sonuç → sınırlılık veya eleştiri**. Bu iskeleti tanırsan soruların çoğunun cevabını nerede arayacağını önceden bilirsin.

Temel ilke: **Cevap metindedir.** Genel kültürünle doğru olan ama metinde dayanağı olmayan şık yanlıştır. Süreyi de planla: 80 soruluk sınavda okuma için metin başına **yaklaşık 10 dakika** (4 soru) ayır; bir soruda 3 dakikayı geçiyorsan işaretle ve ilerle.

## Örnekler
- *What is the passage mainly about?* — Metin esas olarak ne hakkındadır? (ana fikir)
- *According to the passage, the bacteria become active when water enters a crack.* — Metne göre bakteriler bir çatlağa su girdiğinde etkinleşir. (detay)
- *It can be inferred from the passage that the method may save money in the long run.* — Yöntemin uzun vadede para kazandırabileceği çıkarılabilir. (çıkarım)
- *The word 'which' refers to calculating the exact paths.* — 'which' kesin yörüngeleri hesaplamayı kastediyor. (gönderim)
- *The author mentions the football match in order to give an example.* — Yazar maçtan örnek vermek için söz eder. (amaç)
- *Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage?* — Metinde hangisine değinilmemiştir?

## Nasıl çözülür
1. **Önce soru kökünü oku**, metni sonra. Kök tipini belirle: *mainly about / best title* = ana fikir, *according to* = detay, *inferred / implied* = çıkarım, *refers to* = gönderim, *closest in meaning* = bağlamda anlam, *in order to* = amaç, *NOT mentioned* = değinilmeyen.
2. Kökteki **anahtar kelimeyi** (sayı, özel ad, terim) seç ve metinde tara. Kelime metinde eş anlamlısıyla geçebilir: *closed* ↔ *sealed*, *cheap* ↔ *inexpensive*.
3. **Paragrafın yapısını** gör: ilk cümle konu, *however / yet / nevertheless* sonrası yazarın asıl vurgusu, son cümle genellikle sonuç ya da uyarıdır. Ana fikir ve tutum soruları bu üç noktadan çözülür.
4. Anahtar kelimenin geçtiği cümleyi ve bir önceki/sonraki cümleyi dikkatle oku; şıkları bu bölümle tek tek karşılaştır.
5. Çeldiricileri türüne göre ele: aşırı genelleme, kısmen doğru, metindeki kelimeyi tekrar eden ama anlamı bozan şık, zıt anlam.
6. *NOT mentioned* sorusunda her şıkkı metinde bul ve işaretle; metinde karşılığı bulunmayan tek şık cevaptır.

**Örnek çözüm:** Metin: beyaz boya ile çatı sıcaklığı düşüyor; *The effect on outdoor air temperatures, however, was much smaller.* Soru: *According to the passage, painting the roofs white ----.* Adım 1: detay sorusu. Adım 2: anahtar kelime *painted the roofs*. Adım 4: sonraki cümle üst kat sıcaklığının iki derece düştüğünü söylüyor. Adım 5: 'made outdoor air two degrees cooler' şıkkı *two degrees* kelimesini tekrar ediyor ama dış havaya uyguluyor; *however* cümlesi bunun tersini söylüyor. Cevap: 'lowered temperatures on the top floors'.

## Tuzaklar ve sık yapılan hatalar
- **Aşırı genelleme:** Metin *some, may, often* derken şık *all, always, never, completely* der. Bu şıklar neredeyse her zaman yanlıştır.
- **Kısmen doğru şık:** Şıkkın ilk yarısı metinle uyuşur, ikinci yarısı uydurmadır. Şıkkı sonuna kadar oku.
- **Kelime tekrarı tuzağı:** Metindeki *forty percent, Southern Hemisphere* gibi ifadeleri aynen taşıyan ama başka bilgiye bağlayan şık. Tanıdık kelime görmek doğruluk kanıtı değildir.
- **Zıt anlam:** *however* öncesi ile sonrası karıştırılırsa yazarın görüşünün tam tersi seçilir.
- **Türkçe düşünme hatası:** *modest* her zaman 'alçakgönüllü' değildir; metinde 'sınırlı, beklenenden az' demektir. Kelimeyi sözlükteki ilk anlamıyla değil, cümledeki işleviyle çöz.

## Sınav ipucu
Fen metinlerinde sayılara takılma; sorular genellikle sayının kendisini değil, karşılaştırmayı sorar (*twice as fast, less than a tenth*). Tutum sorularında araştırmacıların *admit, stress, warns against* gibi fiillerine bak: bunlar 'temkinli' bir tutumun işaretidir. Metne başlamadan önce dört sorunun köklerine hızla göz atmak, okurken neyi arayacağını bilmeni sağlar ve metin başına 10 dakikalık süreyi rahatça korur.

exercises.question: Even a coin-sized piece of space ---- can seriously damage a working satellite.

membrane
limestone
consultation
coverage

exercises.question: Because the model's forecasts were ---- on days with unusual events, planners could not depend on them.
options: straightforward
reassuring
inexpensive
unreliable

exercises.question: Herbs and young salad leaves bring high profits, but ---- foods such as wheat and potatoes are too cheap to grow indoors.
options: porous
staple
dormant
overlapping
standardised

exercises.question: The researchers warned that the results, though ----, should not be taken as proof that mining is harmless.
options: unreliable
inactive
sobering
scattered
reassuring
exercises.explanation: 'Though' ile kurulan karşıtlık, sonuçların rahatlatıcı olduğunu ama yine de güvence sayılmaması gerektiğini anlatır; doğru cevap 'reassuring'. 'Sobering' (düşündürücü, kaygı verici) seçilseydi uyarıyla karşıtlık oluşmazdı; 'inactive' sonuçlar için kullanılmaz.

exercises.passage: Engineers had expected a simple installation, but the project turned out to be far less straightforward than the company had advertised.
exercises.question: The word 'straightforward' in the sentence is closest in meaning to ----.
options: profitable
simple
popular
visible
modern

exercises.passage: After the first year, the vertical farm's success proved more modest than its founders had hoped: it covered its costs but made almost no profit.

options: shy

exercises.passage: Concrete is the most widely used building material on Earth, yet it has a serious weakness: tiny cracks. Water enters these cracks, reaches the steel bars inside and causes them to rust, which gradually weakens the whole structure. Engineers at a small materials laboratory in northern Europe have been testing a possible solution. They mix dormant bacteria and a source of calcium into fresh concrete. As long as the concrete stays dry, the bacteria remain inactive. When a crack forms and rainwater seeps in, however, the microbes wake up and produce limestone, which gradually seals the gap. In laboratory tests, cracks up to half a millimetre wide were closed within three weeks. The method is not yet ready for large projects, mainly because the special ingredients make the concrete about forty percent more expensive. Nevertheless, the team argues that the extra cost could be recovered over time, since bridges and tunnels built with the material would need far fewer repairs.
exercises.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: the reasons why the steel bars inside bridges and tunnels rust much faster than engineers expected
the rising cost of building materials in northern Europe
a type of concrete that can repair its own cracks with the help of bacteria
the different kinds of bacteria that live in rainwater
a new method for producing limestone in factories
exercises.explanation: Metin, bakteriler sayesinde çatlaklarını kendisi kapatan betonu anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'a type of concrete that can repair its own cracks…'. Çeliğin paslanması yalnızca sorunun girişidir, ana konu değildir; kireçtaşı üretimi ise yöntemin bir parçasıdır, fabrikada üretim söz konusu değildir.

exercises.passage: On hot summer afternoons, city centres are often several degrees warmer than the countryside around them. This effect, known as the urban heat island, is largely caused by dark surfaces such as asphalt roads and tar roofs, which absorb sunlight during the day and release heat at night. In one medium-sized city, local authorities decided to test a simple solution. Over two summers, they painted the roofs of three hundred public buildings with a bright white paint that reflects most of the sunlight. Sensors placed inside the buildings showed that indoor temperatures on the top floors fell by an average of two degrees, and electricity use for air conditioning dropped noticeably. The effect on outdoor air temperatures, however, was much smaller and difficult to measure. Researchers believe that a far larger share of the city's roofs would have to be painted before people in the streets felt any real difference. They also point out that white paint loses some of its brightness as dust and dirt build up on it.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Why Asphalt Roads Should Be Banned
How Air Conditioning in Public Buildings Creates Urban Heat Islands
The Countryside: Warmer Than Expected
Dust and Dirt as the Main Cause of Urban Heat
Cooler Roofs, Cooler Rooms: Testing White Paint in a City
exercises.explanation: Metin bir şehirde çatıları beyaza boyama denemesini ve içerideki serinlemeyi anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'Cooler Roofs, Cooler Rooms…'. Asfaltın yasaklanması önerilmiyor; kırsalın daha sıcak olduğu da metnin tam tersidir.

exercises.passage: For coastal communities without rivers or reliable rainfall, turning seawater into drinking water is often the only option. Large desalination plants, however, consume enormous amounts of electricity and are usually too costly for isolated villages. A research group working with a fishing community on a dry island has been testing a device that relies solely on sunlight. Seawater flows slowly across a dark, porous sheet, which absorbs heat and warms a thin layer of water. The vapour then passes through a membrane and condenses on a cooler surface underneath, leaving the salt behind. Because the device has no moving parts, it requires little care, and villagers were trained to clean the membranes themselves within a single afternoon. A unit the size of a dining table currently produces around twenty litres of fresh water on a sunny day, which is enough for the basic needs of a small household but far from enough for agriculture. The researchers admit that output drops sharply on cloudy days. Still, they regard the device as a promising addition to, rather than a replacement for, existing water sources such as rainwater tanks.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why dry islands rarely receive enough rainfall
the high electricity costs of the large desalination plants that supply drinking water to cities
a solar-powered device that produces drinking water from seawater on a small scale
a programme that teaches fishermen to build rainwater tanks
the use of desalinated water to irrigate crops on islands
exercises.explanation: Metnin büyük bölümü güneşle çalışan küçük bir tuzdan arındırma cihazını anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'a solar-powered device…'. Büyük tesislerin elektrik maliyeti yalnızca girişte geçer; tarım için yeterli olmadığı açıkça söylendiğinden sulama şıkkı yanlıştır.

exercises.passage: Thousands of pieces of old satellites and rocket stages now circle the Earth at speeds of several kilometres per second. Even a piece of debris the size of a coin can damage a working satellite, so space agencies keep detailed catalogues of the objects they can follow. Until recently, such tracking depended on a handful of large and expensive radar stations. A university consortium has now proposed a different approach: linking dozens of small, inexpensive radar receivers spread across several continents. Each receiver on its own is too weak to locate small debris accurately, but when their signals are combined by software, the network can detect objects that the large stations sometimes miss. In a six-month test, it identified more than four hundred pieces that did not appear in any public catalogue. Critics note that the system still struggles to calculate the exact paths of these objects, which is what satellite operators actually need in order to avoid collisions. The consortium accepts this limitation but argues that knowing an object exists is the necessary first step. It plans to add more receivers, particularly in the Southern Hemisphere, where coverage has traditionally been poor.
exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: explain why old satellites break into pieces
describe a low-cost network for detecting space debris and its current limitations
argue that the large and expensive radar stations should be closed down and replaced by small receivers
compare the public catalogues of different space agencies
warn that collisions in space have become unavoidable
exercises.explanation: Metin ucuz alıcılardan oluşan ağı, sonuçlarını ve eleştirilen eksiğini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'describe a low-cost network…'. Büyük radarların kapatılması önerilmiyor; çarpışmaların kaçınılmaz olduğu da söylenmiyor, bu aşırı bir yorumdur.

exercises.passage: In recent years, a growing number of municipalities have paid for so-called digital twins: detailed computer models of a city that are continuously updated with data from traffic sensors, energy meters and weather stations. Supporters claim that such models allow planners to test a decision before it is put into practice. Before closing a street to cars, for instance, officials could simulate the likely effect on bus timetables, air quality and nearby shops. The appeal is obvious, yet the experience of an early user, a mid-sized port city, suggests that the benefits are less straightforward than advertised. Its model, launched with considerable publicity, predicted traffic flows with impressive accuracy on ordinary days. On days with unusual events, such as a football match combined with heavy rain, its forecasts proved unreliable, precisely when planners needed them most. exercises.passage: Scattered across parts of the deep ocean floor lie potato-sized lumps known as nodules. They contain manganese, nickel and cobalt, metals in heavy demand for batteries, and several companies hope to collect them with robotic vehicles. Much of the scientific debate has focused on the direct damage such vehicles would cause to the seabed, where nodules grow by only a few millimetres per million years and where many animals live attached to them. A less visible concern, however, is the cloud of fine mud that mining would stir up. To estimate how far such plumes might travel, an international team released a small, controlled amount of mud at a depth of four thousand metres and monitored it with sensors for several weeks. The plume did not rise towards the surface, as some had feared; instead, most of it settled within a few hundred metres. Yet a thin, barely detectable portion drifted more than five kilometres before coming to rest. The researchers stress that their experiment was tiny compared with commercial operations, which could disturb thousands of square kilometres over decades. Whether the thin, far-travelling layer harms filter-feeding animals, which depend on clean water to capture food particles, remains unknown. For this reason, the team warns against interpreting their reassuring short-range results as evidence that mining would be harmless.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the commercial value of metals used in modern batteries
an experiment investigating how far mud stirred up by deep-sea mining might spread
the reasons why nodules grow by only a few millimetres per million years on the ocean floor
the design of robotic vehicles that collect nodules
the feeding habits of animals that live in shallow waters
exercises.explanation: Metnin merkezinde madencilikle kalkacak çamur bulutunun ne kadar uzağa gidebileceğini ölçen deney var; doğru cevap 'an experiment investigating how far mud … might spread'. Metallerin değeri ve nodüllerin yavaş büyümesi giriş bilgisidir; sığ sular hiç anılmaz.

exercises.passage: Vertical farms grow leafy vegetables indoors, on shelves stacked several metres high, under LED lights. Because the climate inside is fully controlled, they need no pesticides, use up to ninety-five percent less water than open fields and can be located close to the supermarkets they supply. For these reasons, they were widely celebrated a decade ago as the future of urban food production. The reality has been more modest. A study of indoor farms in one country found that roughly a third of those opened in the past ten years had closed. The main difficulty is energy: replacing the sun with lamps is expensive, and when electricity prices rose sharply, many farms could no longer sell their lettuce at competitive prices. The farms that survived tend to share two features. They concentrate on high-value crops such as herbs and young salad leaves rather than staple foods like wheat or potatoes, and they have signed long-term contracts for renewable electricity at fixed prices. Analysts conclude that vertical farming is unlikely to replace traditional agriculture but may occupy a profitable niche.
exercises.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: the reasons why vertical farms use far less water and land than traditional open fields
a new type of LED light designed for growing vegetables
the difficulties vertical farms have faced and the features of those that have survived
the rising price of lettuce in supermarkets
a government plan to replace traditional agriculture
exercises.explanation: Metin dikey tarımın beklenen başarıyı gösterememesini ve ayakta kalan çiftliklerin ortak özelliklerini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'the difficulties vertical farms have faced…'. Daha az su kullanımı yalnızca giriş bilgisidir; geleneksel tarımın yerini alması ise metinde olası görülmüyor.

exercises.passage: Measuring how quickly mountain glaciers are shrinking has traditionally required researchers to walk across the ice, drilling holes and inserting stakes whose exposed length is checked each year. The method is accurate but slow, dangerous and limited to a few glaciers that are easy to reach. In an isolated mountain range, a team of glacier scientists has been testing small drones that fly over the ice and take thousands of overlapping photographs. Software then combines the images into a three-dimensional map with a precision of a few centimetres. By comparing maps made in successive summers, the team can calculate how much ice has been lost across an entire glacier rather than at a handful of stakes. The results were sobering: the glaciers studied lost ice almost twice as fast as the stake measurements had suggested, mostly in heavily cracked areas that researchers on foot had avoided for safety reasons. The drones are not without problems. Strong winds keep them on the ground on many days, and their batteries run down quickly in the cold. Nevertheless, the team believes that combining occasional field visits with regular drone flights offers the most complete picture.
exercises.question: The author's main purpose in the passage is to ----.
options: argue that researchers should stop walking on glaciers
explain why mountain glaciers in the isolated range have started to grow again in recent summers
describe the dangers of using drones in cold weather
compare different software programs used to make maps
show how drones have improved the measurement of ice loss on glaciers
exercises.explanation: Metin drone fotoğraflarıyla tüm buzulun ölçülebildiğini ve önceki yöntemin kaçırdığı kaybı gösterdiğini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'show how drones have improved the measurement…'. Ekip saha ziyaretlerinin sürmesini istiyor; buzulların büyüdüğü ise zıt anlamdır.

Nevertheless, the team believes that combining occasional field visits with regular drone flights offers the most complete picture.
exercises.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage?
options: The drones are too expensive for most research teams.
Strong winds prevent the drones from flying on many days.
The drones' batteries run down quickly in the cold.
The stake method can be used only on glaciers that are easy to reach.
The three-dimensional maps are accurate to within a few centimetres.
exercises.explanation: Rüzgâr ve pil sorunu, kazık yönteminin kolay ulaşılan buzullarla sınırlı olması ve haritaların birkaç santimetrelik hassasiyeti metinde geçiyor. Drone'ların maliyetinden hiç söz edilmiyor; doğru cevap 'The drones are too expensive for most research teams.'

exercises.passage: Products labelled 'biodegradable' are often assumed to vanish harmlessly wherever they end up. In practice, the label usually means that the material breaks down under specific conditions, typically in industrial composting facilities where temperatures exceed fifty degrees and microbes are abundant. To find out what happens elsewhere, marine scientists placed samples of five common biodegradable plastics in mesh bags on the seabed of a sheltered bay, alongside samples of ordinary plastic. After eighteen months, the results varied widely. One material, made from a substance produced by bacteria, had largely disappeared. Two others had lost less than a tenth of their mass and looked almost unchanged, while the remaining two had broken into small pieces that were still clearly plastic. The ordinary plastic, as expected, showed no measurable change. The authors warn that fragmentation should not be mistaken for degradation: smaller pieces can be swallowed more easily by marine animals. They recommend that labels should state the conditions under which a product actually degrades, and that consumers should not assume that a biodegradable bag thrown into the sea will behave like a fallen leaf.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

Ordinary plastic actually breaks down faster in the sea than the plastics labelled biodegradable.
Industrial composting facilities should be built near the sea.

Plastics labelled biodegradable do not all break down in the sea, so their labels can be misleading.

exercises.passage: As electric vehicles multiply, so does the number of batteries that will eventually reach the end of their useful lives. Most current recycling plants shred old batteries and then either melt the pieces at high temperatures or dissolve them in strong acids. Both routes recover valuable metals such as cobalt and nickel efficiently, but lithium, the element that gives these batteries their name, is often lost in the waste or recovered only at a cost higher than its market price. A pilot plant run by a regional engineering school is experimenting with an alternative called direct recycling. Instead of breaking the electrode material down into its constituent elements, the process aims to restore it, replenishing the lithium that was lost during use and returning the material to manufacturers in a form ready for new batteries. The appeal lies in the energy saved: repairing a damaged crystal is far less demanding than manufacturing one from raw ingredients. The difficulty is variety. Battery chemistries have changed several times over the past fifteen years, and a process designed for one type of electrode cannot simply be applied to another. Unless manufacturers agree on more standardised designs, or batteries carry clear information about their contents, direct recycling may remain confined to the small market of carefully sorted waste.

options: the reasons why electric vehicles are becoming more popular
the market price of lithium compared with cobalt and nickel
the dangers of dissolving batteries in strong acids
a recycling method that restores battery material and the obstacle that limits its use
a new design for electric vehicle batteries that will never need to be recycled or replaced

units.title: Okuma kampı 2: sağlık
units.description: Gerçek YDS uzunluğunda sağlık ve biyoloji metinleriyle okuma pratiği
units.guide:
## Strateji
Sağlık ve yaşam bilimleri metinleri YDS'nin en sık okuma konularındandır. Bu metinlerin dili **temkinlidir**: araştırmacılar kesin konuşmaz, *suggest, appear to, may, is associated with, is linked to* gibi ifadeler kullanır. Soruların çoğu bu temkini yakalayıp yakalamadığını ölçer. Metin *may reduce* diyorsa *always cures* diyen şık, metin *is associated with* diyorsa *causes* diyen şık yanlıştır.

Bu metinler çoğunlukla şu sırayı izler: **yaygın inanış veya sorun → çalışma (kimlerle, ne kadar sürede, nasıl) → bulgu → sınırlılık (küçük örneklem, kısa süre, öz bildirim) → öneri**. Detay soruları bulgu kısmından, çıkarım ve tutum soruları sınırlılık ve öneri kısmından gelir. Süre hedefin yine metin başına **yaklaşık 10 dakika**: 1 dakika soru köklerini tara, 4 dakika metni oku, 5 dakikada soruları çöz.

## Örnekler
- *Feeling lonely was strongly associated with heart disease.* — Yalnızlık hissi kalp hastalığıyla güçlü biçimde ilişkiliydi. (ilişki var; neden-sonuç kanıtlanmadı)
- *The molecules appear to strengthen the lining of the intestine.* — Moleküller bağırsak zarını güçlendiriyor gibi görünüyor. (temkinli bulgu)
- *None of these has been tested in animals, let alone in humans.* — Bunların hiçbiri hayvanlarda bile denenmedi, insanlarda denenmesi şöyle dursun.
- *The study was too short to show long-term effects.* — Çalışma uzun vadeli etkileri göstermek için çok kısaydı. (sınırlılık)
- *Sceptics point out that pain was measured only through patients' own reports.* — Şüpheciler ağrının yalnızca hastaların kendi bildirimiyle ölçüldüğüne dikkat çekiyor. (eleştiri)

## Nasıl çözülür
1. **Soru kökünü önce oku** ve tipini işaretle (ana fikir, detay, çıkarım, gönderim, bağlamda anlam, amaç/tutum, *NOT mentioned*).
2. Kökteki **anahtar kelimeyi** belirle ve metinde tara: *fibre, nap, loneliness* gibi terimler ya da *after three weeks, eighty percent* gibi sayılar.
3. **Paragrafın yapısını** çıkar: çalışma hangi cümlede başlıyor, bulgu nerede, *however / but / sceptics* ile sınırlılık nerede veriliyor?
4. Şıkları **kesinlik derecesine** göre karşılaştır: metindeki *may, some, slightly* ifadesini şıkta *always, all, greatly* diye değiştiren şıkkı ele.
5. **İlişki-neden ayrımı** yap: metin yalnızca ilişki kuruyorsa *X causes Y* diyen şık yanlıştır.
6. Çıkarım sorusunda seçtiğin şıkkı destekleyen cümleyi metinde gösterebiliyor musun? Gösteremiyorsan şık yorumdur, çıkarım değildir.

**Örnek çözüm:** Metin: yalnız yaşamak hastalıkla zayıf, yalnızlık hissi kalp hastalığıyla güçlü biçimde ilişkili. Soru: *It can be inferred from the passage that ----.* Adım 3: sonuç cümlesi *loneliness is not simply the same as being alone*. Adım 4–5: 'living alone causes heart disease' şıkkı hem neden-sonuç kuruyor hem de metnin söylediğinin tersini söylüyor. 'Increasing social contacts will cure loneliness' aşırı genelleme. Doğru şık: 'people can feel lonely even when they are often with others' — metindeki *surrounded by others yet still feel lonely* ifadesiyle desteklenir.

## Tuzaklar ve sık yapılan hatalar
- **Neden-sonuç tuzağı:** *associated with / linked to* ilişkiyi gösterir. Türk adaylar bunu çoğu zaman 'neden olur' diye okur.
- **Kesinliği artıran şık (aşırı genelleme):** *The nap improved memory in all students* gibi. Metin genç ve sağlıklı gönüllülerle sınırlıysa bu genelleme yanlıştır.
- **Kısmen doğru şık:** Bulgunun ilk yarısı doğru, ikinci yarısı uydurma (*fibre increased bacterial variety and cured inflammation*).
- **Metindeki kelimeyi tekrarlayan şık:** *forty minutes, two weeks* gibi sayıları başka bilgiye bağlayan şık. Sayı tanıdık diye işaretleme.
- **Zıt anlam:** *Surprisingly, the extra study time gave almost no advantage* cümlesini atlayan aday 'more study = better results' şıkkına düşer.
- **Genel kültür tuzağı:** 'Lif sağlıklıdır' bildiğin bir bilgidir; ama soru metnin ne dediğini sorar, senin ne bildiğini değil.

## Sınav ipucu
Sağlık metinlerinde son iki cümleye özellikle dikkat et: araştırmacıların uyarısı (*caution, stress, warn*) ve önerisi (*recommend, advise*) neredeyse her zaman bir soruya dönüşür. Tutum sorusunda 'cautious, careful, measured' gibi temkin bildiren şıklar sık doğru çıkar; 'enthusiastic' ya da 'dismissive' gibi uç tutumlar ancak metin açıkça öyleyse doğrudur.

exercises.text: After a few weeks, the novelty of the new desks began to ___ off.
exercises.translation: Birkaç hafta sonra yeni masaların yenilik çekiciliği geçmeye başladı.

exercises.question: Because hearing loss develops slowly and without pain, it often goes ---- until it is too late.
options: ineffective
mild
unnoticed
tropical
unfamiliar
exercises.explanation: Ağrısız ve yavaş gelişen bir sorun 'fark edilmeden' ilerler; 'go unnoticed' kalıbıyla doğru cevap 'unnoticed'. 'Ineffective' (etkisiz) ve 'mild' (hafif) 'go' fiiliyle bu anlamı kurmaz.

exercises.question: None of the new substances has been tested on animals, ---- on human patients.
options: let alone
by default
in itself
accordingly
rule of thumb
exercises.explanation: 'Hayvanlarda bile denenmedi, insanlarda denenmesi şöyle dursun' anlamı 'let alone' ile kurulur; doğru cevap 'let alone'. 'Accordingly' (dolayısıyla) bir sonuç bildirir ve olumsuz bir kıyas kurmaz; 'by default' ise 'varsayılan olarak' demektir.

exercises.question: Giving patients a fake drug while telling them it is real involves ----, which most medical codes do not allow.
options: circulation
nourishment
attractiveness
deception
audibility
exercises.explanation: Sahte ilacı gerçek diye vermek 'aldatma'dır; doğru cevap 'deception'. 'Circulation' (kan dolaşımı) ve 'nourishment' (besin) etik bir sorunu anlatmaz.

exercises.question: Insecticides gradually lose their power because mosquito populations ---- resistance to them.
options: forbid
evolve
digest
outweigh
drown out
exercises.explanation: Sivrisinek popülasyonları zamanla direnç 'geliştirir'; doğru cevap 'evolve'. 'Forbid' (yasaklamak) bir canlı topluluğu için anlamsızdır; 'outweigh' (ağır basmak) bir karşılaştırma bildirir.

exercises.question: The district decided that the health benefits of a later start ---- the practical problems it caused for families.
options: shrank
adjusted
sprayed
mated
outweighed
exercises.explanation: Faydaların sorunlardan 'ağır bastığı' için okul saatinin korunduğu anlaşılıyor; doğru cevap 'outweighed'. 'Shrank' (küçüldü) nesne almaz; 'adjusted' (uyum sağladı) da iki şeyi kıyaslamaz.

exercises.passage: Separating male mosquitoes from females by hand is laborious, so the laboratory needs dozens of trained technicians.
exercises.question: The word 'laborious' in the sentence is closest in meaning to ----.
options: completely free of risk
requiring a lot of time and effort
cheap, quick and simple to carry out
impossible to measure
easy to automate
exercises.explanation: Düzinelerce teknisyen gerektiren bir işin 'zahmetli, emek isteyen' olduğu anlaşılır; doğru cevap 'requiring a lot of time and effort'. 'cheap, quick and simple to carry out' zıt anlamdır; 'easy to automate' ise cümledeki elle yapılan iş vurgusuyla çelişir.

exercises.passage: The music in the café was so loud that it drowned out our conversation, and we had to go outside to talk.
exercises.question: The phrase 'drowned out' in the sentence is closest in meaning to ----.
options: made more interesting
recorded secretly
ended politely
made impossible to hear
made shorter
exercises.explanation: Dışarı çıkıp konuşmak zorunda kalındığına göre müzik konuşmayı 'duyulmaz hale getirmiştir'; doğru cevap 'made impossible to hear'. 'Made more interesting' bağlamla çelişir; 'drown' (boğulmak) kelimesinden yola çıkıp sonu anlatan 'ended politely' gibi şıklara gitmek tipik bir tuzaktır.

exercises.passage: Many students believe that staying up late to study is the best way to prepare for an exam. A study at a teacher-training college suggests otherwise. Researchers divided ninety volunteers into three groups and asked them to learn a list of unfamiliar words in the early afternoon. One group then took a forty-minute nap, the second watched a nature documentary, and the third continued studying the same list. When all participants were tested that evening, the nappers remembered about fifteen percent more words than either of the other groups. Surprisingly, the extra study time gave the third group almost no advantage. The researchers suggest that sleep helps the brain move new information from short-term to long-term storage. However, they point out that their volunteers were young and healthy, and that a long nap late in the day may make it harder to fall asleep at night. They therefore recommend short naps taken soon after learning, rather than long ones in the evening.
exercises.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: the best way to watch documentaries while studying
the reasons why students stay up late before exams
a study showing that a short sleep after learning can improve memory
the health problems caused by sleeping too little
a new teaching method that was developed and tested at a teacher-training college
exercises.explanation: Metin öğrenmeden sonra kısa bir kestirmenin hatırlamayı artırdığını gösteren çalışmayı anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'a study showing that a short sleep after learning can improve memory'. Geç saate kadar çalışma yalnızca giriş cümlesidir; yeni bir öğretim yönteminden söz edilmiyor.

exercises.passage: Many students believe that staying up late to study is the best way to prepare for an exam. A study at a teacher-training college suggests otherwise. Researchers divided ninety volunteers into three groups and asked them to learn a list of unfamiliar words in the early afternoon. One group then took a forty-minute nap, the second watched a nature documentary, and the third continued studying the same list. When all participants were tested that evening, the nappers remembered about fifteen percent more words than either of the other groups. Surprisingly, the extra study time gave the third group almost no advantage. The researchers suggest that sleep helps the brain move new information from short-term to long-term storage. However, they point out that their volunteers were young and healthy, and that a long nap late in the day may make it harder to fall asleep at night. They therefore recommend short naps taken soon after learning, rather than long ones in the evening.
exercises.question: The researchers recommend that people who want to remember new information ----.

exercises.passage: The human gut is home to trillions of bacteria, many of which help to break down food that our own bodies cannot digest. Dietary fibre, found in vegetables, beans and whole grains, is one of their main sources of nourishment. When the bacteria ferment fibre, they produce small molecules that appear to strengthen the lining of the intestine and reduce inflammation. In a twelve-week study, sixty adults who normally ate little fibre were asked to double their intake gradually. Tests showed that the variety of their gut bacteria increased within a month. Several participants, however, complained of bloating and discomfort during the first two weeks, and four left the study for this reason. The researchers note that the gut community needs time to adjust, which is why they advise people to add fibre to their diet slowly rather than all at once. They also stress that the study was too short to show whether the changes lead to better health in the long run.
exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Why Beans Are Bad for Digestion
The Hidden Dangers of the Trillions of Bacteria in the Human Body
A Diet Without Fibre Is the Healthiest
How to Lose Weight in Twelve Weeks
More Fibre, More Gut Bacteria: But Go Slowly
exercises.explanation: Metin lif alımının bağırsak bakterilerinin çeşitliliğini artırdığını ama yavaş artırılması gerektiğini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'More Fibre, More Gut Bacteria: But Go Slowly'. Metne göre bakteriler faydalıdır, tehlikeli değil; lifsiz diyet önerisi ise zıt anlamdır.

exercises.passage: Most antibiotics in use today were discovered in the middle of the twentieth century, largely from microbes living in soil. Since then, the search for new ones has slowed, partly because the same substances keep being rediscovered. A national project has tried to widen the search by involving secondary-school pupils. Over three years, more than two thousand classes collected soil from gardens, riverbanks and school playgrounds and sent it to a central laboratory. There, technicians grew the bacteria in each sample and tested whether they could stop the growth of common disease-causing strains. Around one sample in forty contained a microbe with some antibacterial activity, and a handful produced substances that did not match anything previously known. None of these has yet been tested in animals, let alone in humans, and the organisers are careful to point out that most promising substances fail long before they reach patients. The project's value, they argue, lies not only in its scientific results but also in showing young people how research is actually done.
exercises.question: The passage mainly describes ----.
options: the history of the first antibiotics that were discovered in soil in the middle of the twentieth century
a new antibiotic that has been successfully tested on patients
a project in which school pupils helped search for new antibiotics in soil
the dangers of soil bacteria found in school playgrounds
the training of laboratory technicians in secondary schools
exercises.explanation: Metin öğrencilerin toprak örnekleri topladığı ulusal antibiyotik arama projesini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'a project in which school pupils helped search for new antibiotics in soil'. Hiçbir madde henüz hastalarda denenmedi; bu şık zıt bilgi veriyor. Yirminci yüzyıl yalnızca giriş bilgisidir.

exercises.passage: It has long been known that people with close social ties tend to live longer, but the reasons are still debated. One explanation is behavioural: people who live with others may be reminded to take their medicine, eat regular meals and see a doctor when they feel unwell. Another is biological: long-lasting loneliness may keep the body in a state of mild stress, raising blood pressure and weakening the immune response. A long-term study of four thousand adults over the age of sixty-five tried to separate these explanations. Participants reported how lonely they felt and how often they saw friends or relatives, and their health was followed for eight years. Living alone in itself was only weakly linked to illness. Feeling lonely, on the other hand, was strongly associated with heart disease, even among participants who had frequent visitors and followed their doctors' advice. The authors conclude that loneliness is not simply the same as being alone, and that programmes which only increase the number of social contacts may miss people who are surrounded by others yet still feel lonely.
exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: People who live alone always become ill more often than those who live with friends or relatives.
The feeling of loneliness, rather than living alone, appears to be linked to heart disease.
Older adults should be forced to live with their relatives.
Taking medicine regularly prevents all kinds of heart disease.
Social contacts have no effect on how long people live.
exercises.explanation: Çalışma yalnız yaşamanın hastalıkla zayıf, yalnızlık hissinin ise kalp hastalığıyla güçlü biçimde ilişkili olduğunu buldu; doğru cevap 'The feeling of loneliness, rather than living alone, appears to be linked to heart disease.' 'Always become ill' aşırı genellemedir ve metindeki 'only weakly linked' ifadesiyle çelişir.

exercises.passage: For decades, the placebo effect has been treated as a nuisance in medical research: patients who receive a sugar pill often report real improvements, which makes it harder to measure the true benefit of a new drug. Recently, however, some researchers have begun to ask whether the effect could be used on purpose. The obvious objection is ethical. Giving patients a fake treatment while telling them it is real involves deception, which most medical codes forbid. A clinic specialising in long-term back pain therefore tested an unusual alternative: 'open-label' placebos, which patients knowingly take. Half of the participants received their usual care, while the other half were also given a bottle clearly marked 'placebo pills' and told honestly that the capsules contained no active ingredient but that similar pills had helped some people in earlier studies. After three weeks, the placebo group reported clearly less pain and better sleep than the comparison group. Sceptics point out that pain was measured only through patients' own reports, which are easily influenced by expectations and by the extra attention participants received. The researchers accept this point and are now planning a study that will also record measurable outcomes such as how far patients can walk. Even if the effect turns out to be small, they argue, a treatment that is cheap, honest and free of harmful effects deserves serious investigation.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why sugar pills are harmful to patients who suffer from long-term back pain
the history of medical codes that forbid deception
a trial testing whether placebos can help patients even when they know the pills are fake
a new drug for back pain that has no side effects
the way doctors measure pain in hospitals
exercises.explanation: Metin hastaların plasebo olduğunu bildiği hapların ağrıya etkisini test eden çalışmayı anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'a trial testing whether placebos can help patients even when they know the pills are fake'. Kapsüllerde etkin madde yoktur, dolayısıyla yeni bir ilaç söz konusu değildir; tıbbi etik kurallar yalnızca bağlamdır.

Even if the effect turns out to be small, they argue, a treatment that is cheap, honest and free of harmful effects deserves serious investigation.
exercises.question: Sceptics criticise the study mainly because ----.
options: the patients were not told the truth about what the capsules actually contained
the results depended on what patients themselves said about their pain
the study did not include a comparison group
the pills caused sleep problems
too many patients left the study early
exercises.explanation: Şüpheciler ağrının yalnızca hastaların kendi bildirimleriyle ölçüldüğünü vurguluyor; doğru cevap 'the results depended on what patients themselves said about their pain'. Hastalara dürüstçe bilgi verildiği için 'the patients were not told the truth…' diyen şık metinle çelişir; karşılaştırma grubu da vardır.

exercises.passage: For decades, the placebo effect has been treated as a nuisance in medical research: patients who receive a sugar pill often report real improvements, which makes it harder to measure the true benefit of a new drug. Recently, however, some researchers have begun to ask whether the effect could be used on purpose. The obvious objection is ethical. Giving patients a fake treatment while telling them it is real involves deception, which most medical codes forbid. A clinic specialising in long-term back pain therefore tested an unusual alternative: 'open-label' placebos, which patients knowingly take. Half of the participants received their usual care, while the other half were also given a bottle clearly marked 'placebo pills' and told honestly that the capsules contained no active ingredient but that similar pills had helped some people in earlier studies. After three weeks, the placebo group reported clearly less pain and better sleep than the comparison group. Sceptics point out that pain was measured only through patients' own reports, which are easily influenced by expectations and by the extra attention participants received. The researchers accept this point and are now planning a study that will also record measurable outcomes such as how far patients can walk. Even if the effect turns out to be small, they argue, a treatment that is cheap, honest and free of harmful effects deserves serious investigation.
exercises.question: The researchers' attitude towards the criticism can best be described as ----.
options: defensive, since they refuse to change their methods or to plan any further studies
indifferent, since they ignore the sceptics completely
angry, since they believe the sceptics are dishonest
confused, since they do not understand the objection
open, since they accept it and plan to include measurable outcomes
exercises.explanation: Araştırmacılar eleştiriyi kabul edip yürüme mesafesi gibi ölçülebilir sonuçları da kaydedecek bir çalışma planlıyor; doğru cevap 'open, since they accept it…'. 'Refuse to change their methods' zıt anlamdır.

exercises.passage: Mosquitoes that carry dengue fever have proved remarkably difficult to control. Insecticides lose their power as mosquito populations evolve resistance, and spraying also kills harmless insects. On a small tropical island, health officials have been trying a biological approach instead. Each week, they release several hundred thousand male mosquitoes that have been infected in the laboratory with a common bacterium. Male mosquitoes do not bite, so the releases pose no direct risk to residents. When these males mate with wild females, however, the resulting eggs fail to hatch, and the population gradually shrinks. After two years, mosquito numbers in the treated villages had fallen by around eighty percent compared with untreated villages, and reported dengue cases declined accordingly. The programme is not without difficulties. Separating males from females in the laboratory is laborious, and even a small number of accidentally released females could spread the bacterium into the wild population, making the method ineffective. Moreover, the island's isolation makes it unusually suitable: on a mainland, mosquitoes from untreated areas would constantly fly in and replace those that had disappeared. Officials on the island are nevertheless encouraged and have asked neighbouring islands to organise their own releases, arguing that cooperation would protect the progress already achieved.
exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: explain why insecticides are the best way to control mosquitoes
describe a biological method of reducing mosquito numbers and the conditions it depends on
warn residents of the island about the dangers of male mosquitoes
compare dengue fever with other tropical diseases
argue that the method should immediately be used on every mainland, where it would work even better
exercises.explanation: Metin bakteriyle enfekte erkek sivrisinek salımını, sonuçlarını ve adaya özgü koşullara bağlılığını anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'describe a biological method…'. Erkek sivrisinekler ısırmadığından risk yoktur; anakaraya uygulanması ise metne göre zordur, bu yüzden 'used on every mainland' diyen şık zıt anlamdır.

exercises.passage: Office workers often spend more than nine hours a day sitting, a habit linked to weight gain and poor circulation. In response, many employers have bought height-adjustable desks that allow staff to work standing up. A company with three large offices decided to measure whether these desks actually changed behaviour. Half of its employees received adjustable desks; the others kept their ordinary ones. During the first month, the desk users stood for nearly two hours a day on average. By the sixth month, however, this had fallen to less than forty minutes, and many had stopped standing altogether. Interviews revealed that the novelty had worn off and that some employees found standing tiring by the afternoon. A smaller group who also received a short reminder on their computer screens every hour kept standing for much longer. The study's authors conclude that equipment alone rarely changes habits; it needs to be combined with simple signals that turn the new behaviour into part of the daily routine.
exercises.question: What is the passage mainly about?
options: the health dangers of standing up for too many hours a day at an adjustable office desk
a company that banned sitting in its offices
a study showing that adjustable desks alone did not change office workers' habits for long
the reasons why employees prefer ordinary desks
a new kind of computer screen that reduces weight gain
exercises.explanation: Çalışma ayarlanabilir masaların etkisinin zamanla azaldığını ve yalnızca hatırlatmayla korunduğunu gösteriyor; doğru cevap 'a study showing that adjustable desks alone did not change … habits for long'. Ayakta durmanın tehlikesi ana konu değildir; oturmanın yasaklanması da söz konusu değil.

exercises.passage: Hearing specialists have become increasingly concerned about young people who listen to music through headphones for several hours a day. Unlike an injury, noise-induced hearing loss develops slowly and without pain, so it often goes unnoticed until it is irreversible. In a survey of one thousand university students, nearly a third reported occasional ringing in their ears after listening to music, an early warning sign of damage. When their devices were checked, many were found to be playing music at levels well above those recommended for long periods. Interestingly, students who used noise-cancelling headphones listened at lower volumes, apparently because they no longer needed to drown out the traffic and conversation around them. The researchers do not recommend that young people give up headphones. Instead, they suggest following a simple rule of thumb: if someone standing next to you can hear your music, it is too loud. They also call on manufacturers to include volume limits that are switched on by default rather than hidden deep in the settings menu.
exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Headphones should be banned for university students.
Noise-cancelling headphones are the main cause of hearing loss among university students who listen to music.
Hearing loss caused by noise is always painful.
Ringing in the ears is a sign of good hearing.
Many young people listen to music loudly enough to risk permanent hearing damage, but simple steps can reduce the risk.
exercises.explanation: Metin gençlerin yüksek sesle müzik dinlemesinin kalıcı kayıp riski taşıdığını ve basit önlemler önerildiğini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'Many young people listen to music loudly enough…'. Araştırmacılar kulaklıktan vazgeçmeyi önermiyor; gürültü engelleyici kulaklıklar ise tam tersine daha düşük sesle kullanılıyor.

exercises.passage: Birds that live in cities face a problem their rural relatives do not: the constant low rumble of traffic. Because many birds use song to defend their territory and attract mates, being heard is essential. A team of biologists recorded the songs of a common songbird in a large city and in nearby forests. City birds sang at a noticeably higher pitch, which allows their songs to rise above the low-frequency noise of engines. They also began singing earlier in the morning, before the rush hour started. What remains unclear is whether these differences are learned or passed on from parents. To investigate, the researchers raised young birds from city nests in quiet aviaries far from any road. Several of them still developed higher-pitched songs, suggesting that at least part of the change may have a genetic basis. The authors caution, though, that the number of birds was small. They also note a possible cost: females in some species prefer males with lower songs, which are often a sign of a larger body. If so, city males may be trading attractiveness for audibility.
exercises.question: The passage mainly discusses ----.
options: why birds that live in quiet forests sing more beautifully and more often than birds in cities
the effect of traffic noise on human sleep
the number of songbirds living in large cities
how biologists build aviaries for young birds
how city birds change their songs to be heard over traffic noise and what this may cost them
exercises.explanation: Metin şehir kuşlarının trafik gürültüsünü aşmak için daha tiz ve erken öttüğünü ve bunun olası bedelini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'how city birds change their songs…'. Kafes yapımı yalnızca deneyin bir aşamasıdır; ötüşün güzelliğinden söz edilmiyor.

exercises.passage: Teenagers are often criticised for staying up late and struggling to get up in the morning. Sleep researchers, however, argue that this pattern is largely biological: during puberty, the body begins to release the sleep hormone melatonin later in the evening, shifting the natural time of falling asleep by up to two hours. Early school start times therefore force many teenagers to wake up before their bodies are ready. When one school district moved the start of its secondary schools from 7.45 to 8.50, researchers compared students' sleep and performance before and after the change. Students did not, as some parents had predicted, simply go to bed later; on average they gained around forty minutes of sleep per night. Attendance in the first lesson improved, and fewer students reported feeling sleepy in class. Grades rose slightly, although the authors warn that other changes in the district during the same period make it difficult to attribute this improvement to the new timetable alone. The reform also had costs: bus routes had to be redesigned, and some parents found it harder to combine the later start with their own working hours. Even so, the district has decided to keep the new schedule, arguing that the benefits for students' health outweigh the practical inconvenience.

options: to criticise teenagers for going to bed late
to explain how melatonin is produced in adults
to argue that school buses should start running much earlier in the morning
to describe the effects of moving school start times later for teenagers
to show that grades depend only on sleep
exercises.explanation: Metin okul başlangıç saatinin ertelenmesinin uyku, devam ve notlar üzerindeki etkisini ve maliyetlerini anlatıyor; doğru cevap 'to describe the effects of moving school start times later for teenagers'.
